overall.assessment: Prema navedenoj strukturi, podcast uglavnom predstavlja kršćanski usklađenu antropologiju: poduzetništvo, kreativnost i rad prikazani su kao darovi i odgovornosti, a ne samo kao sredstva osobnog uspjeha; to odgovara katoličkom razumijevanju rada kao sudjelovanja u stvaranju i služenja općem dobru. Obitelj, vjera, glazba i potraga za precima proširuju priču izvan ekonomskog postignuća prema odnosima, zahvalnom pamćenju i pripadnosti, dok govor o talentima i strahu od propuštene prilike dobro pristaje biblijskom pozivu na odgovorno korištenje darova. Važna ograda jest da sam popis tema ne pokazuje koliko se uspjeh povezuje sa služenjem siromašnima i zajedničkom dobru, a pojedini motivi — osobito rodno podijeljene uloge, usporedba Hrvatske sa Švicarskom i naglasak na poduzetničkoj inicijativi — mogu zvučati pojednostavljeno ako se ne uravnoteže dostojanstvom i pozivom svake osobe te solidarnošću. Stoga je ukupni dojam pretežno pozitivan i ohrabrujući, ali na temelju tematskog pregleda, a ne cjelovitog prijepisa, ne može se pouzdano procijeniti nijansa svake izjave ni koliko su društvene posljedice rada i poslovanja razrađene.
seeds_of_logos: Poduzetništvo i dizajn prikazani kao kreativno razvijanje primljenih darova; crkveni nauk o radu također ga vidi kao sudjelovanje u Božjem stvaralačkom djelu, uz odgovornost za opće dobro.

Teme talenata, hrabrosti i straha od propuštene prilike mogu potaknuti na odgovornu inicijativu umjesto pasivnog čuvanja onoga što je povjereno; evanđeoska prispodoba upozorava da darovi trebaju donositi plod.
Roditeljstvo prikazano kroz djecu koja ljubav uče promatrajući roditelje: naglasak je na svjedočanstvu, svakodnevnom odnosu i oblikovanju osobe, a ne samo na verbalnim poukama.
Vjera kao orijentir koji nadilazi karijeru, uz pokušaj povezivanja poslovnih odluka s odgovornošću pred Bogom; to može čuvati poduzetništvo od svođenja na samopotvrđivanje ili profit.
Potraga za obiteljskim korijenima i pamćenje predaka mogu njegovati zahvalnost, međugeneracijsku povezanost i poštovanje ljudskih životnih priča, bez svođenja osobe na njezino podrijetlo.
Poziv na ohrabrivanje drugih — „Bravo, brate, kreni!“ — suprotstavlja se zavisti i društvenom obeshrabrivanju te može izgrađivati kulturu potpore i susreta.

PDV i računovodstvena odgovornost tematizirani poslovnim žargonom, ali načelno upućuju na to da vjera i zakonsko-građanska odgovornost nisu erdvasta područja; sam tematski pregled ipak ne omogućuje procjenu pojedinosti stava.
concerns: Podjela „lovac u šumi“ i „čuvarica četiri kuta kuće“ može, ako je iznesena kao opće pravilo, učvrstiti krute rodne stereotipe i zasjeniti dostojanstvo, sposobnosti i slobodu razlučivanja pojedinih žena i muškaraca. Iz same oznake teme nije moguće zaključiti je li riječ o osobnom obiteljskom modelu ili univerzalnoj normi.

Poduzetnički uspjeh, hrabrost i samodisciplina mogu postati preusko mjerilo ljudske vrijednosti ako se ne povežu s dostojanstvom radnika, pravednim uvjetima rada, odgovornim korištenjem dobiti i brigom za siromašne. Katolički socijalni nauk naglašava da poduzetnici i radnici trebaju pridonositi zajedničkom dobru, a promicanje siromašnih ne svodi se na osobni uspjeh ili kratkoročnu pomoć.

Poruka da bi Hrvatska „mogla biti Švicarska“ može biti poticaj na društvenu odgovornost, ali može i svesti dobrobit zajednice na bogatstvo, produktivnost ili usporedbu s drugom državom ako se ne razjasni što se smatra istinskim napretkom.

Pozivanje na „talente“ i strah od propuštene prilike može ohrabriti inicijativu, ali treba paziti da se ne protumači kao tvrdnja kako su svi neuspjesi posljedica nedostatka hrabrosti ili truda; prikaz teme ne upućuje na to da podcast takvu tvrdnju izričito zastupa.

Tematski pregled ne pokazuje je li potraga za korijenima predstavljena uz kršćansku nadu i dostojanstvo svih predaka ili se ponegdje pretvara u idealiziranje obiteljske prošlosti; ni taj mogući rizik ne treba pripisivati podcastu bez uvida u cijeli razgovor.
overall.theological_context: Prispodoba o talentima u Mt 25 pruža prikladan biblijski okvir za teme darova, inicijative i odgovornosti, ali njezin smisao nije samo osobno postignuće: kršćanska plodnost uključuje služenje drugima, a posebno neindiferentnost prema siromašnima. U okviru KKC-a, navedeni su relevantni odlomci o poštovanju tuđe imovine (2407–2414), ljubavi prema siromašnima (2443–2449) i ljudskoj solidarnosti (1939–1942); oni poslovni uspjeh usmjeravaju prema pravednosti i zajedničkom dobru. Crkveni naglasak na radu kao sudjelovanju u stvaranju dodatno traži da poduzetnička kreativnost promiče dostojanstven rad i prava radnika, a ne samo rast poslovanja.

overall.assessment_en: According to the stated structure, the podcast mostly presents a Christian-aligned anthropology: entrepreneurship, creativity, and work are presented as gifts and responsibilities, and not merely as means of personal success; this corresponds to the Catholic understanding of work as participation in creation and service to the common good. Family, faith, music, and the search for ancestors broaden the story beyond economic achievement toward relationships, grateful memory, and belonging, while speaking of talents and the fear of a missed opportunity fits well with the biblical call to the responsible use of gifts. An important caveat is that the list of topics itself does not show how much success is connected with service to the poor and the common good, and individual motifs — especially gender-divided roles, the comparison of Croatia with Switzerland, and the emphasis on entrepreneurial initiative — may sound oversimplified if they are not balanced with the dignity and vocation of each person and with solidarity. Therefore, the overall impression is predominantly positive and encouraging, but based on a thematic overview rather than a complete transcript, the nuance of each statement cannot be reliably assessed, nor how elaborated the social consequences of work and business are.
overall.theological_context_en: The parable of the talents in Mt 25 provides a suitable biblical framework for the themes of gifts, initiative, and responsibility, but its meaning is not merely personal achievement: Christian fruitfulness includes service to others, and especially non-indifference toward the poor. Within the framework of the CCC, relevant passages on respect for the goods of others (2407–2414), love for the poor (2443–2449), and human solidarity (1939–1942) are cited; they direct business success toward justice and the common good. The Church's emphasis on work as participation in creation further requires that entrepreneurial creativity promote dignified work and workers' rights, and not merely business growth.
seeds_of_logos_en: Entrepreneurship and design presented as the creative development of received gifts; the Church's teaching on work also sees it as participation in God's creative work, along with responsibility for the common good.

The themes of talents, courage, and fear of a missed opportunity can encourage responsible initiative instead of passive safeguarding of what has been entrusted; the Gospel parable warns that gifts ought to bear fruit.
Parenthood presented through children who learn love by observing their parents: the emphasis is on witness, everyday relationship, and the formation of the person, not merely on verbal instructions.

Faith as a point of reference that transcends career, with an attempt to connect business decisions with responsibility before God; this can safeguard entrepreneurship from being reduced to self-affirmation or profit.
The search for family roots and remembering ancestors can cultivate gratitude, intergenerational connection, and respect for human life stories, without reducing a person to their origin.
The call to encourage others — "Bravo, brother, go for it!" — opposes envy and social discouragement and can build a culture of support and encounter.

VAT and accounting responsibility addressed in business jargon, but in principle indicating that faith and legal-civic responsibility are not separate domains; the thematic overview itself, however, does not allow for an assessment of the specifics of the stance.
concerns_en: The division of "hunter in the woods" and "keeper of the four corners of the house" can, if presented as a general rule, reinforce rigid gender stereotypes and overshadow the dignity, abilities, and freedom of discernment of individual women and men. From the topic label alone, it is not possible to conclude whether this is a personal family model or a universal norm.

Entrepreneurial success, courage, and self-discipline can become too narrow a measure of human worth if they are not connected with the dignity of workers, just working conditions, the responsible use of profit, and care for the poor. Catholic social teaching emphasizes that entrepreneurs and workers should contribute to the common good, and the promotion of the poor is not reduced to personal success or short-term assistance.

The message that Croatia "could be Switzerland" can be an incentive for social responsibility, but it can also reduce the well-being of the community to wealth, productivity, or comparison with another state if what is considered true progress is not clarified.

Appealing to "talents" and the fear of a missed opportunity can encourage initiative, but care should be taken that it is not interpreted as an assertion that all failures are the result of a lack of courage or effort; the presentation of the topic does not indicate that the podcast explicitly advocates such an assertion.

The thematic overview does not show whether the search for roots is presented alongside Christian hope and the dignity of all ancestors, or if it turns somewhere into an idealization of the family past; neither should that potential risk be attributed to the podcast without insight into the entire conversation.

sections.subtitle: Od plastelina do obiteljske tvornice čokolade
sections.screenshot_description: Fran Petar Reizl opisuje svoje rano stvaralaštvo i put prema dizajnu
sections.content:
Novu epizodu podcasta **Redefinicija** voditelj **Kruno** otvara pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip“. Gost je **Fran Petar Reizl**, kojega predstavlja kao poduzetnika, pokretača brenda **Reizl Snacks**, dizajnera, grafičara i glazbenika. Kao najvažnije uloge ističe one supruga i oca četvero djece. Gost zahvaljuje na pozivu i kaže da je počašćen što može biti dio „jedne sekvence dobrih podcasta“.

Kruno podsjeća da je Fran s poduzetništvom počeo vrlo mlad te ga moli da opiše svoje formativno razdoblje, sve do obiteljskog brenda **Vrsna čokolada**. Fran objašnjava da je oduvijek bio netko tko stvara. Otkad zna za sebe igrao se plastelinom i drugim materijalima, a ta se sklonost s vremenom pretvorila u dizajn. Najprije ga je upisao u srednjoj školi, a zatim i na studiju.

Nakon tri godine fakulteta shvatio je, kako kaže, da „nije stvoren samo za sjediti i nešto učiti“, nego da naučeno treba vraćati svijetu. U isto su vrijeme njegovi roditelji razmišljali o promjenama u maloj obiteljskoj tvrtki u **Sesvetama**. Zajedno su izradili projekt za **europske fondove** uz jasan dogovor: ako prođe, krenut će, a ako ne prođe, „nikom ništa“. Projekt je, kako Fran kaže, „hvala Bogu“ ne samo prošao, nego su bili i „jako obilato ohrabreni“. Tako je počela proizvodnja čokolade.

Vrsna čokolada i danas uspješno posluje i raste, što gostu posebno znači jer je riječ o domaćem, obiteljskom brendu. Kroz šest do sedam godina u toj tvrtki učio je o proizvodnim procesima, računovodstvu i svemu što poduzetnik mora proći. To ga je pripremilo za samostalan iskorak prije tri godine, kada je pokrenuo Reizl Snacks.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje kreativnost, pošten rad, poduzetničku inicijativu i skrb za obitelj kao vrijedne ljudske djelatnosti te izražava zahvalnost Bogu. Ne iznosi značajne tvrdnje o vjeri koje bi proturječile Svetom pismu ili katoličkom nauku.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk prepoznaje stvaralaštvo i poduzetničku inicijativu kao moguće oblike ljudskog rada i sudjelovanja u Božjem djelu, pod uvjetom da služe stvarnim potrebama i dobru osobe i zajednice. Rad također može pridonositi uzdržavanju i stabilnosti obitelji; zato je važno da poslovni uspjeh ostane povezan s pravednošću i poštovanjem ljudskog dostojanstva.

sections.subtitle_en: From plasticine to a family chocolate factory
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran Petar Reizl describes his early creativity and journey toward design
sections.content_en:
Host **Kruno** opens the new episode of the podcast **Redefinicija** with the greeting „Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph“. The guest is **Fran Petar Reizl**, whom he introduces as an entrepreneur, founder of the brand **Reizl Snacks**, designer, graphic artist, and musician. As the most important roles, he highlights those of husband and father of four children. The guest thanks for the invitation and says he is honored to be able to be part of „a sequence of good podcasts“.

Kruno recalls that Fran started with entrepreneurship very young and asks him to describe his formative period, all the way to the family brand **Vrsna čokolada**. Fran explains that he has always been someone who creates. For as long as he can remember, he played with plasticine and other materials, and over time that inclination turned into design. First he enrolled in it in high school, and then also in university.

After three years of college, he realized, as he says, that he „was not made just to sit and learn something“, but that what was learned should be given back to the world. At the same time, his parents were thinking about changes in the small family company in **Sesvete**. Together they developed a project for **European funds** with a clear agreement: if it passes, they will start, and if it does not pass, „no harm done“. The project, as Fran says, „thank God“ not only passed, but they were also „very abundantly encouraged“. That is how chocolate production began.

Vrsna čokolada still operates successfully and grows today, which means a lot to the guest especially because it is a domestic, family brand. Over six to seven years in that company, he learned about production processes, accounting, and everything an entrepreneur must go through. This prepared him for an independent step forward three years ago, when he launched Reizl Snacks.

sections.subtitle: Reizl Snacks: zdravija alternativa i četiri strgana blendera
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje razvoj voćnih pločica i testiranje smjese
sections.content:
Fran objašnjava da je Reizl Snacks nastao kao odgovor na nešto što u društvu nedostaje. I mladi i svi koji vole slatko, kaže, hrane se prilično nezdravo. Po njegovu mišljenju čips je pritom najmanji problem. Veći su problem proizvodi s mnogo **prikrivenih tvari** koje su štetne. Ideja je bila povezati se na nov način s ljudima koje poznaju i doći do što boljih sirovina i izvora.

Gost dodaje da mu je kao obiteljskom čovjeku drago što i njegova djeca vide čime se bavi, jer su mu i ona inspiracija. Reizl Snacks opisuje kao tvrtku, start-up i „obiteljski ponos“. Posao je zasad skroman i malen, ali raste, a tržište ga, kako kaže, lijepo prihvaća.

Na Krunino pitanje što brend proizvodi, Fran objašnjava da je Reizl Snacks počeo s čokoladama. Od njih su ipak brzo odustali zbog tehnoloških razloga. Čokolada se topi u transportu, a nisu htjeli da kupci dobiju proizvod kakav ne žele. Slijedila su testiranja, a gost i danas s nevjericom spominje da su „morali proći **četiri strgana blendera**“ dok nisu dobili idealnu smjesu.

Rezultat su **voćne pločice s adaptogenima**, tvarima koje prema gostovu opisu pomažu:
- u detoksikaciji tijela,
- u poboljšanju fokusa,
- u povećanju energije.

Pločice teže samo 20 i 30 grama. Fran ih ugrubo opisuje kao malu voćnu pločicu „punu hranjivih tvari“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: promicanje promišljene prehrane i odgovornosti za zdravlje samo po sebi je dobro, a u tekstu nema tvrdnje koja bi izravno proturječila vjeri ili Svetom pismu. Ipak, navode da adaptogeni pomažu detoksikaciji, fokusu i energiji te da su određene tvari štetne treba shvatiti kao zdravstvene tvrdnje koje ovaj odlomak ne potkrepljuje.
concerns: Pojmovi poput „detoksikacije tijela” i tvrdnje o učinku adaptogena izneseni su bez pojašnjenja ili dokaza; ne treba ih predstavljati kao zajamčene zdravstvene učinke samo na temelju ovog opisa.
Izraz „prikrivene tvari” ostaje neodređen i može ostaviti dojam da su određeni sastojci štetni bez objašnjenja o kojim je tvarima riječ i u kojem kontekstu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk tijelo i zdravlje smatra Božjim darom te potiče razumnu brigu o zdravlju, ali upozorava i na pretjerivanje i kult tijela. Zato je pohvalna briga da hrana bude kvalitetna, ali zdravlje ne treba svoditi na obećanja o energiji, fokusu ili „detoksikaciji”; njega tijela treba ostati razborita i služiti cjelovitom dobru osobe.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is generally aligned with Catholic teaching: promoting mindful nutrition and responsibility for health is good in itself, and there is no claim in the text that would directly contradict the faith or Sacred Scripture. Nevertheless, statements that adaptogens help with detoxification, focus, and energy, and that certain substances are harmful, should be understood as health claims that this passage does not substantiate.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching considers the body and health to be a gift of God and encourages reasonable care for health, but it also warns against exaggeration and the cult of the body. Therefore, concern for food to be of good quality is praiseworthy, but health should not be reduced to promises of energy, focus, or "detoxification"; care of the body must remain prudent and serve the integral good of the person.
concerns_en: Terms like "body detoxification" and claims about the effect of adaptogens are presented without clarification or evidence; they should not be presented as guaranteed health effects solely on the basis of this description.
The phrase "hidden substances" remains vague and may leave the impression that certain ingredients are harmful without explaining which substances are in question and in what context.

sections.subtitle_en: Reizl Snacks: a healthier alternative and four broken blenders
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the development of fruit bars and the testing of the mixture
sections.content_en:
Fran explains that Reizl Snacks came about as a response to something that is missing in society. Both young people and everyone who likes sweets, he says, eat quite unhealthily. In his opinion, chips are the least of the problems here. A bigger problem is products with many **hidden substances** that are harmful. The idea was to connect in a new way with people they know and to obtain the best possible raw materials and sources.

The guest adds that, as a family man, he is glad that his children also see what he does, because they too are an inspiration to him. He describes Reizl Snacks as a company, a start-up, and "family pride". The business is modest and small for now, but it is growing, and the market, as he says, accepts it nicely.

To Kruno's question about what the brand produces, Fran explains that Reizl Snacks started with chocolates. However, they quickly gave up on them for technological reasons. Chocolate melts during transport, and they did not want customers to receive a product they did not want. Testing followed, and the guest still mentions today with disbelief that they "had to go through **four broken blenders**" until they got the ideal mixture.

The result is **fruit bars with adaptogens**, substances that, according to the guest's description, help:
- with body detoxification,
- with improving focus,
- with increasing energy.

The bars weigh only 20 and 30 grams. Fran roughly describes them as a small fruit bar "full of nutrients".

sections.subtitle: Dizajn kao alat: i okus se mora dizajnirati
sections.screenshot_description: Fran objašnjava kako dizajn ulazi u sve sfere ljudskog života
sections.content:
Kruno pita kako Franova dizajnerska podloga utječe na razvoj proizvoda i odnos s kupcima. Gost dizajn opisuje kao „fascinantnu granu“ koja ulazi u sve aspekte ljudskog bitka. Cilj dizajna je stvoriti nešto lijepo i korisno. Da bi se to postiglo, potrebno je mnogo istraživanja, ulaženja u razne sfere društva i razumijevanja različitih ljudi. Svaki je kupac, naglašava, individua sa svojim dostojanstvom i potrebama, na koje proizvođač mora pokušati odgovoriti.

Za Reizl Snacks dizajn je bio ključan jer se, kako kaže, **i okus proizvoda mora dizajnirati**. Trebalo je i procijeniti hoće li proizvod izgledati lijepo ili ružno. Zdravi proizvodi i sušeno voće nisu baš lijepi, iako su vrlo hranjivi. Zato su bili potrebni kompromisi. Fran je svoje znanje iskoristio prije svega za **ambalažu**, koju opisuje kao atraktivnu, modernu i suvremenu, dok je sam proizvod „takav kakav je“.

Gost dodaje da je dizajn jedan od koraka koji su ga doveli do sadašnjeg trenutka. Počelo je kao dječja kreativnost, a postalo profesionalna grana njegova života. Ljudi često misle da se poslovni ljudi bave samo brojkama i postocima. Kao dizajner, međutim, vidi da mnogi zapravo rade na tome da stvore bolje uvjete za druge. U slučaju njegove tvrtke to znači pomoći ljudima da jedu kvalitetnije, odnosno **dizajnirati njihov životni stil i navike**. To naziva holističkim pogledom na posao.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na dostojanstvu svakog kupca, razumijevanju njegovih potreba i stvaranju korisnih proizvoda uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim društvenim naukom, koji čovjeka smatra osobom, a ne pukim sredstvom ili potrošačem. Izraz „dizajnirati životni stil i navike” može biti dobrohotan ako označava ponudu koja podupire dobrobit, ali zahtijeva oprez da se ne pretvori u manipulaciju ili nametanje izbora.
concerns: Odlomak ne razjašnjava kako se oblikuju životne navike kupaca; katolička moralna načela traže poštovanje njihove slobode te odbacuju manipulativno oglašavanje i iskorištavanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk o poslovanju vrednuje proizvode koji istinski služe ljudskim potrebama, a ne potiču potrošnju stvari koje su beskorisne ili štetne; zato su važni stvarna hranjiva vrijednost proizvoda i istinitost poruka na ambalaži. Dostojanstvo kupca uključuje poštovanje njegove slobode i razuma, pa privlačan dizajn treba informirati i privući bez obmanjivanja ili skrivenog utjecaja. Takav pristup može povezati poduzetništvo sa zajedničkim dobrom i razvojem ljudi, umjesto da ih svede na cilj prodaje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on the dignity of every customer, understanding their needs, and creating useful products is largely aligned with Catholic social teaching, which considers the human being a person, and not a mere means or consumer. The expression "to design lifestyle and habits" can be well-intentioned if it signifies an offering that supports well-being, but it requires caution so that it does not turn into manipulation or the imposition of choices.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching on business values products that genuinely serve human needs, rather than encouraging the consumption of things that are useless or harmful; that is why the real nutritional value of the product and the truthfulness of messages on the packaging are important. The dignity of the customer includes respect for their freedom and reason, so attractive design should inform and attract without deception or hidden influence. Such an approach can connect entrepreneurship with the common good and the development of people, instead of reducing them to a sales target.
concerns_en: The passage does not clarify how the lifestyle habits of customers are formed; Catholic moral principles demand respect for their freedom and reject manipulative advertising and exploitation.

sections.subtitle_en: Design as a tool: even taste must be designed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran explains how design enters all spheres of human life
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks how Fran's design background influences product development and the relationship with customers. The guest describes design as a "fascinating branch" that enters all aspects of human being. The goal of design is to create something beautiful and useful. In order to achieve that, a lot of research is needed, entering various spheres of society and understanding different people. Every customer, he emphasizes, is an individual with their own dignity and needs, which the producer must try to respond to.

For Reizl Snacks, design was key because, as he says, **even the taste of the product must be designed**. It was also necessary to assess whether the product would look pretty or ugly. Healthy products and dried fruit are not really pretty, although they are very nutritious. That is why compromises were needed. Fran used his knowledge primarily for the **packaging**, which he describes as attractive, modern, and contemporary, while the product itself is "such as it is".

The guest adds that design is one of the steps that brought him to the present moment. It began as childhood creativity, and became a professional branch of his life. People often think that business people deal only with numbers and percentages. As a designer, however, he sees that many actually work to create better conditions for others. In the case of his company, that means helping people to eat better, that is, **to design their lifestyle and habits**. He calls that a holistic view of business.

sections.subtitle: Lovac u šumi i čuvarica četiri kuta kuće
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o podjeli uloga u braku i kršćanskim vrijednostima
sections.content:
Kruno postavlja pitanje kako uskladiti obiteljski i poslovni život. Fran ga naziva vrlo ozbiljnim pitanjem, koje je dvojbeno i često ostaje bez dobrog javnog odgovora. Kao vjernik vjeruje u **kršćanske vrijednosti**, za koje kaže da su ukorijenjene u prirodnom zakonu. U njegovoj obitelji vrijedi „običan bračni zakon“: muž radi, a žena je više s djecom. On je onaj koji je „na terenu, što bi rekli lovac u šumi“, a supruga brine o „četiri kuta kuće“ i djeci. Naglašava da je i sam vrlo aktivan s djecom, ali kad radi, onda radi.

Gost ne skriva da je takav raspored zahtjevan i da traži žrtvu od oboje. Muž se odriče vremena s djecom i ženom kako bi radio za dobro obitelji. Žena je pak često sama i traži načine kako ispuniti vrijeme i odgajati djecu u dobrom ozračju. Fran to opisuje kao **put posvećenja i svetosti**, koji je u mnogočemu neistražen. Ujedno ga vidi kao priliku da se u modernom dobu razviju dobri mehanizmi za svakodnevni život.

Kruno primjećuje da bi „lijevo-liberalni“ kritičari takav pogled mogli proglasiti toksičnim. Ipak, smatra da model funkcionira ako je riječ o dogovoru u obitelji. Problem nastaje kad muškarac taj dogovor krši i previše se posveti poslu. Fran se slaže i dodaje da neki muškarci rade previše jer su, kako kaže, „nezadovoljeni“ sami sa sobom. Svatko bi trebao raditi onoliko koliko je dobro za obitelj, za njega samog i za posao. Potrebna je **zlatna sredina**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim shvaćanjem braka kao zajedničkog poziva na ljubav, služenje, roditeljsku odgovornost i svakodnevno posvećenje; pritom ispravno naglašava važnost dogovora supružnika i odgovornog usklađivanja rada s obiteljskim dobrom. Ipak, opis muža kao hranitelja i žene kao one koja brine o domu treba shvatiti kao njihov osobni obiteljski raspored, a ne kao obvezan obrazac za sve katoličke obitelji.
concerns: Izrazi „običan bračni zakon” i „lovac u šumi” mogu ostaviti dojam da su takve podjele rada propisane kršćanskim naukom ili prirodnim zakonom; odlomak ne obrazlaže tu tvrdnju niti dovoljno jasno razlikuje osobni izbor od opće norme.
Opis žene kao često same i usmjerene na djecu i kuću može umanjiti važnost uzajamne odgovornosti i zajedničkog sudjelovanja supružnika ako se tumači kao jednostrana ili nepromjenjiva obveza.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk prikazuje brak i obitelj kao put posvećenja koji se živi kroz svakodnevne radosti i žrtve, pa je ta strana odlomka dobro utemeljena. Istodobno, supružnici su pozvani na uzajamnu, nesebičnu ljubav, poštovanje i zajedničko odgovorno odlučivanje, što znači da njihove uloge i raspored rada trebaju služiti dobru oboje i djece. Zato je opisani model prihvatljiv kao dogovor konkretne obitelji, ali nije jedini katolički model: presudni su vjernost bračnom pozivu, briga za djecu i uzajamna potpora, a ne kruta podjela uloga.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage as a shared vocation to love, service, parental responsibility, and daily sanctification; at the same time, it correctly emphasizes the importance of mutual agreement between spouses and responsible balancing of work with the good of the family. However, the description of the husband as the breadwinner and the wife as the one caring for the home should be understood as their personal family arrangement, and not as a mandatory model for all Catholic families.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching presents marriage and the family as a path of sanctification lived through daily joys and sacrifices, so that aspect of the passage is well-founded. At the same time, spouses are called to mutual, selfless love, respect, and joint responsible decision-making, which means that their roles and work schedule should serve the good of both and of the children. Therefore, the described model is acceptable as an agreement of a specific family, but it is not the only Catholic model: fidelity to the marital vocation, care for the children, and mutual support are decisive, rather than a rigid division of roles.
concerns_en: The expressions “ordinary marital law” and “hunter in the forest” can leave the impression that such divisions of labor are prescribed by Christian teaching or natural law; the passage does not substantiate this claim nor does it sufficiently clearly distinguish personal choice from a general norm.

The description of the wife as often alone and focused on the children and the house can diminish the importance of mutual responsibility and shared participation of spouses if interpreted as a one-sided or unchangeable obligation.

sections.subtitle_en: A hunter in the forest and the guardian of the four corners of the house
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the division of roles in marriage and Christian values
sections.content_en:
Kruno poses the question of how to balance family and professional life. Fran calls it a very serious question, which is dubious and often remains without a good public answer. As a believer, he believes in **Christian values**, which he says are rooted in natural law. In his family, an “ordinary marital law” applies: the husband works, and the wife is more with the children. He is the one who is “in the field, as they would say, a hunter in the forest,” and the wife takes care of the “four corners of the house” and the children. He emphasizes that he himself is very active with the children, but when he works, he works.

The guest does not hide that such an arrangement is demanding and that it requires sacrifice from both. The husband gives up time with the children and wife in order to work for the good of the family. The wife, on the other hand, is often alone and seeks ways to fill the time and raise the children in a good atmosphere. Fran describes this as **a path of sanctification and holiness**, which is in many ways unexplored. At the same time, he sees it as an opportunity to develop good mechanisms for everyday life in the modern age.

Kruno observes that “left-liberal” critics could proclaim such a view as toxic. Nevertheless, he considers that the model works if it is an agreement within the family. The problem arises when the man breaks that agreement and dedicates himself too much to work. Fran agrees and adds that some men work too much because they are, as he says, “unsatisfied” with themselves. Everyone should work as much as is good for the family, for himself, and for the job. A **golden mean** is needed.

sections.subtitle: Kraljevstvo Božje umjesto same karijere
sections.screenshot_description: Fran priča o odluci supruge da se posveti djeci
sections.content:
Fran naglašava da se u njegovoj obitelji radi o **velikom sporazumu**. Njegova je supruga profesorica kroatistike i filozofije i imala je uzlaznu karijeru. Kad je stiglo prvo dijete, „prvi mali mačić“, kako ga gost od milja naziva, sama je procijenila koja je njezina uloga. Danas, kaže, sve funkcionira „dosta lijepo“.

Kruno dodaje da su mu mnogi rekli kako u obitelji ništa neće funkcionirati dok muškarac i žena ne osvijeste svoje prave uloge, i s tim se slaže. Navodi i citat koji je čuo: muškarac nije pozvan graditi karijeru, nego **kraljevstvo Božje**. Prema njegovu mišljenju, i u tome treba svakodnevno ciljati zlatnu sredinu.

Fran tu misao razvija. Život traje 80 ili 90 godina i čovjek ga može proživjeti isključivo kroz karijeru, smatrajući je životnim smislom. Može i postaviti nebo kao cilj, a karijeru, koja je potrebna „za kruh svagdašnji“, iskoristiti tako da uz sebe „pokupi cijelu obitelj“. U tom je slučaju, zaključuje, bolje da se obitelj dobro raspodijeli.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da kraljevstvo Božje i vječni cilj imaju prednost pred karijerom te da bračni par treba odgovorno uskladiti posao i obiteljski život uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom i Mt 6,33. Ipak, izrazi o „pravim ulogama” i raspodjeli u obitelji ostaju neodređeni, pa ih ne treba tumačiti kao krute rodne propise ili umanjivanje suprugine slobode i dostojanstva.
concerns: Nije jasno što se podrazumijeva pod „pravim ulogama” muškarca i žene; takva formulacija može sugerirati da postoji samo jedan obvezatan model podjele obiteljskih i profesionalnih dužnosti.

Odluka supruge o karijeri prikazana je kao njezina procjena nakon rođenja djeteta, no katoličko razumijevanje braka poziva na uzajamno odgovorno razlučivanje, a ne na svođenje majčinstva ili očinstva na unaprijed zadanu ulogu.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusov poziv da se najprije traži kraljevstvo Božje daje dobar okvir za tvrdnju da karijera nije konačni smisao života, nego da se rad može usmjeriti služenju Bogu i obitelji (Mt 6,33). Crkva istodobno priznaje osobitu važnost majčine prisutnosti, naročito u prvim mjesecima djetetova života, ali potvrđuje i ženino pravo na obrazovanje, rad i osobne ciljeve. Zato se obiteljska i profesionalna zadaća trebaju skladno usklađivati, uz jednako dostojanstvo i odgovornost muža i žene te uz obostranu brigu za duhovnu i materijalnu dobrobit obitelji.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that the kingdom of God and the eternal goal take precedence over career and that a married couple should responsibly harmonize work and family life is largely in accordance with Catholic teaching and Mt 6:33. However, expressions about "true roles" and distribution in the family remain vague, so they should not be interpreted as rigid gender prescriptions or a diminishing of the wife's freedom and dignity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' call to seek first the kingdom of God provides a good framework for the claim that a career is not the ultimate meaning of life, but that work can be directed toward serving God and family (Mt 6:33). The Church simultaneously recognizes the particular importance of the mother's presence, especially in the first months of a child's life, but also affirms a woman's right to education, work, and personal goals. Therefore, family and professional tasks should be harmoniously balanced, with the equal dignity and responsibility of husband and wife and with mutual care for the spiritual and material well-being of the family.
concerns_en: It is not clear what is meant by "true roles" of man and woman; such a formulation may suggest that there is only one mandatory model for dividing family and professional duties.

The wife's decision regarding her career is presented as her own assessment after the birth of the child, yet the Catholic understanding of marriage calls for mutual responsible discernment, rather than reducing motherhood or fatherhood to a predetermined role.

sections.subtitle_en: The Kingdom of God Instead of Career Alone
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about his wife's decision to dedicate herself to the children
sections.content_en:
Fran emphasizes that in his family, it is a matter of a **great agreement**. His wife is a professor of Croatian language and literature and philosophy and had an upward career. When the first child arrived, "the first little kitten", as the guest affectionately calls him, she evaluated on her own what her role was. Today, he says, everything functions "quite nicely".

Kruno adds that many people told him that nothing in a family will function until a man and a woman become aware of their true roles, and he agrees with that. He also cites a quote he heard: a man is not called to build a career, but **the kingdom of God**. In his opinion, even in that one should aim daily for the golden mean.

Fran develops that thought. Life lasts 80 or 90 years and a person can live it exclusively through a career, considering it the meaning of life. One can also set heaven as the goal, and use a career, which is necessary "for daily bread", in such a way as to "gather the whole family" along with oneself. In that case, he concludes, it is better for the family to distribute itself well.

sections.subtitle: Caru carevo, Bogu Božje: PDV kao dio računice
sections.screenshot_description: Gost iskreno govori o pogrešci pri osnivanju tvrtke i plaćanju PDV-a
sections.content:
Kruno navodi da se na **Konferencijama katoličkih muškaraca** na panelima o leadershipu i poduzetništvu redovito otvara tema poreza. Pita Frana kakav je odnos prema porezu imao kad je kretao praktički od ničega, s obzirom na visoka davanja. Zanima ga je li pomišljao da posluje mimo pravila ili je odlučio „dati Bogu Božje, caru carevo“.

Fran kaže da kod njega nije bilo velike dvojbe jer je znao da mora ići pravim putem. Priznaje i vlastitu pogrešku. Umjesto da posao pokrene kroz obrt ili neki mirniji oblik, odmah je osnovao **d.o.o. u sustavu PDV-a**, pa se prve dvije godine jedva snalazio. Ipak, nikada nije zapao u dugove ni prema državi ni prema suradnicima. PDV danas smatra jednim dijelom računice.

Gost otvoreno priznaje da je plaćanje PDV-a neugodno. U sebi se pita zašto se toliko bori za nešto, a onda četvrtinu daje „nečemu što ne vidi“, pa i stvarima s kojima se ne slaže nužno. Unatoč tome poštuje **Isusov naputak** o caru i Bogu i smatra ga posve konstruktivnim. Tko god radi procjenu projekta ili troškovnik, od kupovine do vođenja tvrtke, može u nju ugraditi „tu četvrtinu koja nije tvoja“. Poslovanje se, kaže, i dalje može dobro razvijati.

Na kraju prenosi „pošalicu“ hrvatskih povratnika iz **Amerike i Australije**: tko prođe test na hrvatskom tržištu, spreman je za bilo koje tržište. Fran to doživljava kao izazov. Ako uspije u Hrvatskoj, moći će i dalje. Kruno se slaže da je to „dobar test“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: gost odbacuje poslovanje mimo pravila, prihvaća obvezu plaćanja poreza i primjereno povezuje tu dužnost s Isusovim riječima o caru i Bogu. Njegovo priznanje da mu je porez neugodan i da se ne slaže nužno sa svim javnim izdacima izražava osobni prigovor, ali ne dovodi u pitanje obvezu plaćanja.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da su plaćanje poreza i poštovanje zakonite vlasti moralne dužnosti povezane sa suodgovornošću za opće dobro, a ne samo praktičan trošak poslovanja. Isusov poziv da se caru da carevo ne znači da je svaki postupak vlasti pravedan: građanska vlast mora služiti općem dobru, a poslušnost ima granice kad bi značila sudioništvo u zlu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: the guest rejects doing business outside the rules, accepts the obligation to pay taxes, and appropriately connects this duty with Jesus' words about Caesar and God. His admission that tax is unpleasant to him and that he does not necessarily agree with all public expenditures expresses a personal objection, but does not call into question the obligation to pay.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that paying taxes and respecting legitimate authority are moral duties linked to co-responsibility for the common good, not just a practical cost of doing business. Jesus' call to give to Caesar what is Caesar's does not mean that every action of the authorities is just: civil authority must serve the common good, and obedience has limits when it would mean complicity in evil.

sections.subtitle_en: To Caesar what is Caesar's, to God what is God's: VAT as part of the calculation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks honestly about a mistake when founding a company and paying VAT
sections.content_en:
Kruno states that at the **Catholic Men's Conferences**, the topic of taxes is regularly raised on panels about leadership and entrepreneurship. He asks Fran what his attitude toward taxes was when he was starting from practically nothing, considering the high levies. He wonders whether he thought of doing business outside the rules or decided to „give to God what is God's, to Caesar what is Caesar's“.

Fran says that there was no great doubt for him because he knew he had to take the right path. He also admits his own mistake. Instead of starting the business through a trade or some calmer form, he immediately founded a **d.o.o. in the VAT system**, so for the first two years he barely managed. Still, he never fell into debt either to the state or to his associates. Today, he considers VAT to be one part of the calculation.

The guest openly admits that paying VAT is unpleasant. Inwardly, he wonders why he fights so hard for something, and then gives a quarter to „something he does not see“, even to things with which he does not necessarily agree. Despite that, he respects **Jesus' instruction** about Caesar and God and considers it entirely constructive. Whoever does a project estimate or bill of quantities, from purchasing to running a company, can build into it „that quarter that is not yours“. Business, he says, can still develop well.

In the end, he conveys a „joke“ of Croatian returnees from **America and Australia**: whoever passes the test on the Croatian market is ready for any market. Fran perceives this as a challenge. If he succeeds in Croatia, he will be able to go further. Kruno agrees that it is a „good test“.

sections.subtitle: Talenti kao Božji alat i strah od propuštene prilike
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o pozivu, talentima i želji da bude primjer svojoj djeci
sections.content:
Kruno pita što Frana svakog jutra pokreće da bude kreativan i odakle mu ideje za nove proizvode, s obzirom na veliku konkurenciju i brojne „omče“ i „utege“ u poduzetništvu. Fran kaže da je pitanje jednostavno, ali odgovor složen. Pokreće ga kombinacija **poziva koji mu je Bog dao** i talenata koje je dobio. Dugo mu je trebalo da shvati kako ono što je smatrao maštom i fantazijom zapravo jest njegov alat, koji mora koristiti.

Važan je i obiteljski motiv. U braku je šest, gotovo sedam godina i ima četvero djece. Svakodnevno ga potiče misao da će jednog dana biti stariji i gledati ih. Kao otac želi da u njemu vide primjer nekoga „tko nije savršen, ali tko se trudio svaki dan“.

Otkrivajući ljepotu **Božjeg stvaralaštva** u svom životu, u tuđim životima i u svijetu, Fran vidi koliko svatko ima toga dati. Priznaje da se čak boji kako bi bio velik propust kad ne bi reagirao na vrijeme i pustio da ideja „samo tako odleprša“. Poziva se na **Isusovu prispodobu o talentima**. Prva dvojica sluga imala su u sebi „mot“, kako bi rekli na jugu, i krenula raditi. Treći se bojao i propustio priliku pred nosom. To mu je pokretač, ali i način da Bogu zahvali za ono što ima.

Gost dodaje da mnogi poduzetnici vjernici koje poznaje svako jutro razmatraju i mole te se trude živjeti sakramentalno. Ljudi izvana često misle da im se „posrećilo“. Iza uspjeha je, međutim, mnogo plakanja, briga, raspisivanja ideja, dvojbi i **neisplaćenih kredita**, jer žele napraviti nešto bolje od postojećeg stanja. „Dugi odgovor na kratko pitanje“, zaključuje Fran.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: talente prikazuje kao darove za koje smo odgovorni pred Bogom, a prispodobu o talentima povezuje s marljivim služenjem i zahvalnošću. Važna je ipak razlika između razboritog odaziva na dar i pretpostavke da je svaka poduzetnička ideja sigurno Božji poziv ili da je poslovni uspjeh dokaz Božje naklonosti.
concerns: Izraz „poziv koji mu je Bog dao“ može biti osobno svjedočanstvo, ali odlomak ne pojašnjava da se takav poziv razlučuje te da se talenti trebaju koristiti odgovorno i za dobro drugih, a ne samo radi uspjeha.

Strah da će propuštanjem ideje nastati „velik propust“ može potaknuti pretjeranu tjeskobu ako se shvati kao obveza da se provede svaka zamisao; prispodoba poziva na vjernost i plodonosnost, a ne na nepromišljenost.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno tumačenje prispodobe povezuje talente i s osobnim sposobnostima i s pozivom na rad za sebe i za druge; zato kreativnost može biti način služenja bližnjemu, a ne samo sredstvo poslovnog napretka. Kršćanska hrabrost u korištenju darova ne isključuje razborito razlučivanje: poduzetnički rizik nije sam po sebi krepost, nego se procjenjuje prema odgovornosti, pravednosti i dobru koje nastoji ostvariti. Odlomak također dobro ističe očinski primjer; obiteljski život i profesionalni rad mogu biti područja kršćanskog poziva i svjedočenja, a ne suparnici vjeri.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it portrays talents as gifts for which we are accountable before God, and links the parable of the talents with diligent service and gratitude. A distinction is important, however, between a prudent response to a gift and the assumption that every entrepreneurial idea is certainly a calling from God or that business success is proof of God's favor.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's interpretation of the parable connects talents both with personal abilities and with the call to work for oneself and for others; therefore, creativity can be a way of serving one's neighbor, not merely a means of business advancement. Christian courage in using gifts does not exclude prudent discernment: entrepreneurial risk is not in itself a virtue, but is judged according to responsibility, justice, and the good it seeks to achieve. The passage also rightly highlights the fatherly example; family life and professional work can be areas of Christian calling and witness, not rivals to faith.
concerns_en: The phrase “calling that God gave him” may be a personal testimony, but the passage does not clarify that such a calling is discerned and that talents should be used responsibly and for the good of others, not merely for the sake of success.

The fear that letting an idea slip will result in a “great failure” can foster excessive anxiety if understood as an obligation to carry out every idea; the parable calls for faithfulness and fruitfulness, not recklessness.

sections.subtitle_en: Talents as God's Tool and the Fear of a Missed Opportunity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran speaks about calling, talents, and the desire to be an example to his children
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks what drives Fran every morning to be creative and where he gets ideas for new products, given the strong competition and numerous “nooses” and “weights” in entrepreneurship. Fran says the question is simple, but the answer is complex. He is driven by a combination of the **calling that God gave him** and the talents he received. It took him a long time to realize that what he considered imagination and fantasy is actually his tool, which he must use.

The family motive is also important. He has been married for six, almost seven years and has four children. Every day he is encouraged by the thought that one day he will be older and looking at them. As a father, he wants them to see in him an example of someone “who is not perfect, but who tried every day.”

Discovering the beauty of **God's creativity** in his life, in the lives of others, and in the world, Fran sees how much everyone has to give. He admits that he is even afraid that it would be a great failure if he did not react in time and let an idea “just flutter away like that.” He refers to **Jesus' parable of the talents**. The first two servants had the “drive” in them, as they would say in the south, and set to work. The third was afraid and missed the opportunity right in front of his nose. That is his driver, but also a way to thank God for what he has.

The guest adds that many believer-entrepreneurs whom he knows meditate and pray every morning and strive to live sacramentally. People from the outside often think that they “got lucky.” Behind the success, however, is a lot of crying, worries, mapping out ideas, doubts, and **unpaid loans**, because they want to make something better than the existing situation. “A long answer to a short question,” concludes Fran.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija od tri kćeri: djeca uče ljubav gledajući roditelje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira Chestertona o braku kao borbi
sections.content:
Kruno podsjeća da je Franu nedavno stigao četvrti dijete, sin, „napokon, nakon tri djevojčice“. Pita ga koju je najvažniju lekciju naučio u godinama očinstva.

Fran odgovara da je naučio kako će djeca, ako će ljubav od ikoga dobiti, dobiti je od mame i tate. Što je ljubav naučit će također gledajući roditelje i njihov međusobni odnos. Nije tajna, kaže, da je brak „jedno veliko bojno polje“. Citira **Chestertona**, koji je rekao da nitko ne bi trebao ustuknuti pred izazovom braka jer je to doista „borba do smrti“. Fran dodaje: „I doista je.“

Kao najveću lekciju ističe to da djeci mora biti **autentičan i s njima u istini**. Ne očekuje da mu to uzvrate, nego se nada da će to jednog dana moći učiniti na svoj način, za svoje dobro.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da djeca uče ljubav promatrajući odnos roditelja, te da roditelji trebaju biti autentični i iskreni s njima, u skladu je s katoličkim razumijevanjem obitelji i odgoja, u kojem roditeljski primjer ima važnu ulogu. Govor o braku kao „bojnom polju” može se razumjeti kao slikovit opis teškoća i ustrajnosti, a ne kao tvrdnja da su supružnici neprijatelji.
concerns: Izraz „borba do smrti” može zvučati kao da je sukob sama bit braka; teološki je primjerenije razumjeti ga kao borbu protiv sebičnosti, nesporazuma i drugih prepreka ljubavi, a ne kao borbu jednog supružnika protiv drugoga.
Tvrdnju da će djeca ljubav dobiti od mame i tate valja razumjeti kao naglašavanje roditeljske prvenstvene odgovornosti, a ne kao da su roditelji jedini mogući izvor ljubavi, skrbi i odgoja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko učenje podupire važnost roditeljskog primjera: roditelji ne odgajaju djecu samo riječima nego i svjedočanstvom vjernosti, uzajamnog poštovanja i svakodnevne ljubavi. Teškoće u braku ne poništavaju njegovu vrijednost; kršćanska „borba” počinje u supružnicima i obitelji, gdje se nastoje nadvladati sebičnost i nesporazumi te zlo potisnuti obiljem dobra.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that children learn love by observing the relationship of their parents, and that parents should be authentic and honest with them, is in accordance with the Catholic understanding of family and upbringing, in which parental example plays an important role. Speaking of marriage as a "battlefield" can be understood as a vivid description of hardships and perseverance, and not as an assertion that spouses are enemies.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching supports the importance of parental example: parents do not raise children only with words, but also with the witness of fidelity, mutual respect, and daily love. Difficulties in marriage do not negate its value; the Christian "battle" begins within the spouses and the family, where efforts are made to overcome selfishness and misunderstandings and to overcome evil with an abundance of good.
concerns_en: The phrase "fight to the death" can sound as if conflict is the very essence of marriage; it is theologically more appropriate to understand it as a fight against selfishness, misunderstandings, and other obstacles to love, rather than as a fight of one spouse against the other.

The assertion that children will receive love from mom and dad should be understood as an emphasis on the primary responsibility of parents, and not as if parents are the only possible source of love, care, and upbringing.

sections.subtitle_en: A lesson from three daughters: children learn love by watching their parents
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes Chesterton on marriage as a battle
sections.content_en:
Kruno recalls that Fran recently had a fourth child arrive, a son, "finally, after three girls". He asks him what the most important lesson he learned in his years of fatherhood was.

Fran replies that he learned that children, if they will receive love from anyone, will receive it from mom and dad. What love is they will also learn by watching their parents and their mutual relationship. It is no secret, he says, that marriage is "one big battlefield". He quotes **Chesterton**, who said that no one should shrink back from the challenge of marriage because it is truly a "fight to the death". Fran adds: "And it truly is."

As the greatest lesson, he emphasizes that to his children he must be **authentic and with them in truth**. He does not expect them to return this to him, but hopes that one day they will be able to do so in their own way, for their own good.

sections.subtitle: Muževnost kao časno držanje i mudrost znati kada krenuti
sections.screenshot_description: Fran definira muževnost u poslovnom svijetu
sections.content:
Kruno primjećuje da je poslovni svijet uglavnom obojan na muški način. Pita Frana što za njega znači biti muževan u poduzetništvu i leadershipu. Gost kaže da se danas na taj pojam gleda čudno, kao na „čudnovatog kljunaša“ ili „jednoroga, neko mitsko biće“. Mnogi muškarci koje susreće povukli su se u svoju sigurnu zonu. Fali im „kičme“, kako se kaže u narodu, i hrabrosti da stanu iza svojeg „da“ i svojeg „ne“.

Fran kaže da pažljivo bira društvo u poslovnom svijetu. Prema iskustvu s ljudima s kojima se druži, muževnost opisuje kao **časno držanje radi dobra drugih** i bratski stav. Podsjeća da je poduzetništvo često razmjena dobara i da svatko nešto treba. Primjer uzima iz vlastitog posla. Kad traži voće za svoj proizvod, onaj od koga ga traži mora od njega dobiti poštovanje. Uz plaćanje, to znači i ljudsku stranu, primjerice lijepu riječ.

Muževnost vidi i kao nešto što nije podložno političkim pitanjima ni vrijednostima koje „dolaze pa prolaze“. Biti muževan znači biti **čvrsto ukopan u tlu**. Kad bi svi htjeli krenuti, muškarac zna da nije vrijeme. Kad svi stoje, zna krenuti. Zato je **mudrost** po njegovu mišljenju velika sastavnica muževnosti.

U osobnoj noti gost se sjeća predaka o kojima je slušao priče i načina na koji su reagirali u izazovnim situacijama. Spominje i starozavjetne svece i velikane vjere koji su pokazali što znači biti muževan. Upravo to želi prenijeti u svoju poslovnu karijeru.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naglaskom na časti, odgovornosti za druge, pravednosti i mudrosti u poslovanju. Izjednačavanje takvih kreposti s muževnošću može biti poticajno, ali treba paziti da se ne shvati kao tvrdnja da su te kreposti isključivo muške ili da se hrabrost poistovjeti s tvrdoglavošću.
concerns: Izraz da mnogim muškarcima nedostaje „kičme” jest retorička generalizacija, a „čvrsto ukopan u tlu” može se pogrešno shvatiti kao nepopustljivost; kršćanska čvrstina treba biti sjedinjena s razboritošću i pravednošću.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje vodstva u poslu naglašava mudrost i pravednost u konkretnim odnosima te odgovorno služenje ljudima, a ne samo odlučnost ili uspjeh. Crkveni društveni nauk među važnim poslovnim krepostima navodi razboritost pri preuzimanju rizika, pouzdanost, vjernost u odnosima i hrabrost u teškim odlukama.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic emphasis on honor, responsibility for others, justice, and wisdom in business. Equating such virtues with masculinity can be encouraging, but care should be taken not to understand it as a claim that these virtues are exclusively masculine or that courage is equated with stubbornness.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of leadership in business emphasizes wisdom and justice in concrete relationships and responsible service to people, rather than merely decisiveness or success. The Church's social teaching lists among important business virtues prudence in taking risks, reliability, fidelity in relationships, and courage in difficult decisions.
concerns_en: The expression that many men lack a "backbone" is a rhetorical generalization, and "firmly dug into the ground" can be misunderstood as stubbornness; Christian firmness should be united with prudence and justice.

sections.subtitle_en: Masculinity as honorable bearing and the wisdom to know when to move
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran defines masculinity in the business world
sections.content_en:
Kruno notes that the business world is mostly colored in a masculine way. He asks Fran what being masculine in entrepreneurship and leadership means to him. The guest says that today that concept is viewed strangely, like a "platypus" or a "unicorn, some mythical creature." Many men he encounters have retreated into their safe zone. They lack "backbone," as the popular saying goes, and the courage to stand behind their "yes" and their "no".

Fran says that he carefully chooses his company in the business world. According to his experience with the people he associates with, he describes masculinity as **honorable bearing for the good of others** and a brotherly attitude. He recalls that entrepreneurship is often an exchange of goods and that everyone needs something. He takes an example from his own business. When he looks for fruit for his product, the one from whom he seeks it must receive respect from him. Along with payment, that also means the human side, for example, a kind word.

He also sees masculinity as something that is not subject to political issues or values that "come and go." Being masculine means being **firmly dug into the ground**. When everyone would want to move, a man knows that it is not the time. When everyone stands still, he knows how to move. Therefore, in his opinion, **wisdom** is a major component of masculinity.

On a personal note, the guest remembers ancestors about whom he heard stories and the way they reacted in challenging situations. He also mentions Old Testament saints and giants of faith who showed what it means to be masculine. It is precisely this that he wants to carry over into his business career.

sections.subtitle: Nedostaje kultura poticanja: „Bravo, brate, kreni!“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi razgovor s hrvatskim povratnikom koji je radio u Boeingu
sections.content:
Kruno pita s kojim se izazovima danas najviše susreću mladi poduzetnici u Hrvatskoj. Fran prepričava razgovor koji je istog dana imao s Hrvatom povratnikom iz **New Yorka**, koji je radio u **Boeingu**. Sugovornik mu je rekao da su Hrvati koji su otišli u inozemstvo i željeli uspjeti uglavnom natprosječno uspješni jer u sebi imaju borbenost i stav. Oni koji su ostali u Hrvatskoj, smatra gost, često zaborave da se i ovdje moraju boriti i da imaju razloga za samopouzdanje i razvijanje sposobnosti.

Kao objektivne teškoće navodi visok **PDV** i nedostatak poticaja. Financijski poticaji, uključujući one **Europske unije**, postoje. Ono što nedostaje jest poticaj na ljudskoj razini, da netko kaže: „Bravo, brate, kreni, stisni zube, izdrži dvije godine i vidjet ćeš gdje ćeš biti.“ Fali **kultura poticanja**, u kojoj bi otac rekao sinu da krene smjerom koji je zacrtao jer je možda bolji od njegova. Umjesto toga, kaže Fran, često se „povlači za rukav“ uz upozorenja da će se zadužiti i upropastiti sebe i obitelj.

Ipak, vjeruje da ova generacija ima priliku to promijeniti. Velika joj je prednost mnoštvo dobrog i besplatnog sadržaja sa Zapada, osobito o ekonomiji i poduzetništvu, u kojem uspješni ljudi objašnjavaju svoje puteve. Ti su putevi, kaže, „de facto svima isti“: svi krenu od ničega, a ključna je borba. „Tko dulje bude trajao, taj će više toga i postići.“ Hrvatskoj po njegovu mišljenju nedostaje **dugoročni fokus**. Nešto se možda neće riješiti za godinu-dvije, nego za pet, ali nakon pet godina čovjek je već napravio natprosječno mnogo.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim vrednovanjem rada, poduzetničke inicijative, ustrajnosti i potpore mladima, a posebno je pohvalno što ističe ljudsko ohrabrenje i odgovornost prema obitelji. Ipak, tvrdnje da su uspješni poduzetnički putovi „svima isti” i da će više postići onaj tko dulje ustraje mogu zvučati kao da su trud i dugotrajnost dovoljni za uspjeh, što zanemaruje nejednake okolnosti i potrebu da se poslovni ciljevi vode pravednošću i općim dobrom.
concerns: Općenita tvrdnja da svi uspješni kreću od ničega ne uzima u obzir razlike u okolnostima, mogućnostima i obiteljskim obvezama.

Poruka da će onaj tko dulje izdrži više postići može se shvatiti kao obećanje uspjeha ili kao da je poslovni uspjeh mjerilo vrijednosti osobe; katoličko vrednovanje poduzetništva traži i poštovanje ljudskog dostojanstva, pravednost te odgovornost prema zaposlenicima i zajednici.
Ohrabrivanje poduzetničkog rizika ne bi trebalo umanjiti razboritost u zaduživanju i dužnost promišljanja učinaka na obitelj.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk cijeni marljivost i poduzetničku inicijativu: rad može uzdržavati obitelj, razvijati sposobnosti i služiti društvu, a Sveto pismo upozorava na štetnost lijenosti. No uspjeh se ne svodi na profit ili izdržljivost: poduzetničke odluke trebaju poštovati dostojanstvo radnika te biti vođene poštenjem, odgovornošću i brigom za zajednicu. Zato je kultura ohrabrivanja najpotpunija kad uz „kreni i ustraj” uključuje razborito planiranje, prihvaćanje različitih životnih poziva i spremnost da plodove rada dijelimo s drugima.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic valuation of work, entrepreneurial initiative, perseverance, and support for the young, and it is particularly commendable that it emphasizes human encouragement and responsibility toward the family. Nevertheless, claims that successful entrepreneurial paths are “the same for everyone” and that the one who perseveres longer will achieve more can sound as if effort and endurance are sufficient for success, which overlooks unequal circumstances and the need for business goals to be guided by justice and the common good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching values diligence and entrepreneurial initiative: work can support the family, develop abilities, and serve society, and Sacred Scripture warns of the harm of sloth. Yet success is not reduced to profit or endurance: entrepreneurial decisions must respect the dignity of workers and be guided by honesty, responsibility, and care for the community. Therefore, a culture of encouragement is most complete when, alongside “go for it and persevere,” it includes prudent planning, the acceptance of different life vocations, and a readiness to share the fruits of labor with others.
concerns_en: The general claim that all successful people start from nothing does not take into account differences in circumstances, opportunities, and family obligations.

The message that the one who endures longer will achieve more can be understood as a promise of success or as if business success is the measure of a person's worth; the Catholic valuation of entrepreneurship also requires respect for human dignity, justice, and responsibility toward employees and the community.
Encouraging entrepreneurial risk should not diminish prudence regarding indebtedness and the duty to consider the effects on the family.

sections.subtitle_en: A culture of encouragement is missing: “Bravo, brother, go for it!”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys a conversation with a Croatian returnee who worked at Boeing
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks which challenges young entrepreneurs in Croatia face most today. Fran recounts a conversation he had that same day with a Croatian returnee from **New York**, who worked at **Boeing**. His interlocutor told him that Croats who went abroad and wanted to succeed are generally above average in success because they carry fighting spirit and attitude within themselves. Those who stayed in Croatia, the guest believes, often forget that they must fight here as well and that they have reason for self-confidence and developing their abilities.

As objective difficulties he cites high **VAT** and a lack of incentives. Financial incentives, including those of the **European Union**, exist. What is missing is encouragement on a human level, for someone to say: “Bravo, brother, go for it, grit your teeth, endure two years, and you will see where you will be.” A **culture of encouragement** is missing, in which a father would tell his son to head in the direction he mapped out because it is perhaps better than his own. Instead, Fran says, one is often “pulled by the sleeve” with warnings that he will go into debt and ruin himself and his family.

Nevertheless, he believes that this generation has the opportunity to change that. Its great advantage is an abundance of good and free content from the West, especially on economics and entrepreneurship, in which successful people explain their paths. Those paths, he says, are “de facto the same for everyone”: everyone starts from nothing, and the key is the struggle. “Whoever lasts longer, that person will also achieve more.” In his opinion, Croatia lacks a **long-term focus**. Something might not be resolved in a year or two, but in five, but after five years a person has already accomplished above average.

sections.subtitle: Zavist, „naysayeri“ i Hrvatska koja bi mogla biti Švicarska
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o manjku liderstva i nadi u procvat hrvatskog poduzetništva
sections.content:
Kruno nadovezuje da su oko onoga tko kreće u nešto novo obično „naysayeri“, ljudi koji govore: „Nemoj nikako, izgubit ćeš glavu.“ Kao još jednu kočnicu hrvatskog poduzetništva vidi negativnost, a možda i **zavist**. Ako netko krene, drugi će vidjeti da je moguće, pa će i sami morati krenuti. Smatra da previše i previše negativno razmišljamo. S našim talentima i potrebama društva, zaključuje, možemo uspješno odgovoriti na izazove samo ako se malo odvažimo.

Fran se slaže i ponavlja ono što je, kako kaže, govorio i drugdje: Hrvatska je sredina koja bi vrlo lako mogla postati **Švicarska** kad bi to htjela i kad bi imala odgovarajuće liderstvo. Hrvatsko je liderstvo po njegovu sudu generalno loše jer nedostaje ljudi sa stavom, koji se neće podlagati drugima i koji će preuzeti rizike. To je jedan od razloga zašto nije onoliko lako koliko bi moglo biti.

Potvrđuje da su sumnja, nepoticanje i ljubomora definitivno prisutni. Razgovarajući sa starijim, srednjim i mlađim generacijama, kao i s najmlađima koji tek kreću, ipak vidi da stvari idu u dobrom smjeru. Nada se da će se to iskristalizirati i da će Hrvatska doživjeti **procvat**. Kruno se tome iskreno pridružuje.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na poduzetničkoj inicijativi, kreativnosti, razumnom preuzimanju rizika i suzbijanju zavisti uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim socijalnim naukom, koji gospodarsku inicijativu vidi kao mogući doprinos zajednici i odgovoru na ljudske potrebe. Ipak, odlomak ne izriče da uspjeh i razvoj trebaju služiti općem dobru, pa usporedbu s „Švicarskom” valja razumjeti kao ekonomsku sliku, a ne kao cjelovito mjerilo društvenog procvata.
concerns: Rizik i liderstvo nisu sami po sebi kršćanske vrline ako nisu povezani s razboritošću i služenjem drugima; katoličko učenje govori o razumnim rizicima i odgovornosti za dobro zajednice, a ne o uspjehu pod svaku cijenu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička perspektiva poduzetništvo ne odbacuje: kreativna inicijativa može odgovoriti na stvarne potrebe, ali njezin smisao uključuje društvenu odgovornost i služenje, ne samo rast ili dobit. U prispodobi o talentima vjernost može uključivati odvažnost i ulaganje darova, dok biblijska i crkvena predaja zavist prepoznaje kao porok koji čovjeka odvraća od dobra drugoga.
