magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on entrepreneurial initiative, creativity, reasonable risk-taking, and curbing envy is largely aligned with Catholic social teaching, which sees economic initiative as a possible contribution to the community and a response to human needs. However, the passage does not state that success and development should serve the common good, so the comparison with "Switzerland" should be understood as an economic image, and not as a complete measure of societal flourishing.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic perspective does not reject entrepreneurship: creative initiative can respond to real needs, but its meaning includes social responsibility and service, not just growth or profit. In the parable of the talents, faithfulness can include boldness and investing gifts, while biblical and Church tradition recognizes envy as a vice that turns man away from the good of another.
concerns_en: Risk and leadership are not in themselves Christian virtues if they are not linked to prudence and service to others; Catholic teaching speaks of reasonable risks and responsibility for the good of the community, rather than success at all costs.

sections.subtitle_en: Envy, "naysayers", and a Croatia that could be Switzerland
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran speaks about the lack of leadership and hope for the flourishing of Croatian entrepreneurship
sections.content_en:
Kruno adds that around someone starting something new there are usually "naysayers", people who say: "Don't do it at all, you'll lose your head." As another brake on Croatian entrepreneurship, he sees negativity, and perhaps **envy**. If someone starts, others will see that it is possible, so they will have to start themselves too. He believes that we think too much and too negatively. With our talents and the needs of society, he concludes, we can successfully respond to challenges only if we dare a little.

Fran agrees and repeats what, as he says, he has said elsewhere as well: Croatia is an environment that could very easily become **Switzerland** if it wanted to and if it had appropriate leadership. Croatian leadership, in his judgment, is generally bad because there is a lack of people with an attitude, who will not submit to others and who will take risks. That is one of the reasons why it is not as easy as it could be.

He confirms that doubt, lack of encouragement, and jealousy are definitely present. Talking with older, middle, and younger generations, as well as with the youngest who are just starting out, he nevertheless sees that things are going in a good direction. He hopes that this will crystallize and that Croatia will experience a **flourishing**. Kruno sincerely joins in this.

sections.subtitle: Jedna navika, dvije „navikice“: razgovor, rano ustajanje i tišina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost preporučuje razgovor s ljudima od povjerenja i jutarnju tišinu
sections.content:
Na pitanje koju bi naviku preporučio onima koji kreću u poduzetništvo, Fran kaže da je to jedna navika koja povlači još barem dvije „podnaviknice“. Osnovna je navika **puno razgovarati s ljudima u koje imaš pouzdanja**, s onima koji su te dosad poticali i donosili ti vrijednost. S njima treba razglabati ideje kako bi dali dodatni input. Mnogo komunikacije o jednoj temi, objašnjava, otvara mnoga vrata da se plan ostvari u stvarnosti. „Što više vrtimo, to se više šansa povećava.“

To podrazumijeva i određeni životni tempo:
- **ranije ustajanje**,
- **razmišljanje u tišini** prije početka posla,
- raspisivanje misli i njihovo iznošenje pred nekoga od povjerenja.

U tišini i samoći, kaže gost, čovjek puno bolje čuje sam sebe. Najprije treba osvijestiti koje su to misli i zašto se javljaju, zapisati ih, a zatim „staviti na stol“ pred nekoga i prokomentirati. Iako priznaje da je malo zakomplicirao, sažima: teme treba prodiskutirati s onima kojima vjerujemo, jer se tako povećava šansa za uspjeh.

Kruno dodaje da se treba okružiti pametnijima i iskusnijima od sebe. Ljudi se često okružuju onima koji ništa ne znaju o njihovu poslu i koji im „tu i tamo zaplješću“. Zapravo su potrebni **mentori**, od kojih se može učiti. Fran se slaže: „Točno to.“

magisterium.assessment: Savjet o promišljanju u tišini i traženju razboritog savjeta uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim shvaćanjem odgovornog djelovanja: Crkva potiče poduzetnike da zastanu, razmišljaju i donose odluke vođeni savješću, a ne samo aktivizmom ili težnjom za profitom. Odlomak to prikazuje ponajprije kao put prema poslovnom uspjehu, pa bi ga bilo dobro dopuniti razlučivanjem dobra, Božje volje i općega dobra.
concerns: Tvrdnja da se razgovorom povećava šansa za uspjeh može se shvatiti kao praktičan poslovni savjet, ali nije jamstvo uspjeha niti cjelovit kršćanski kriterij za odluku.

Izraz da čovjek u samoći bolje čuje samoga sebe koristan je za samopromišljanje, no katoličko razlučivanje ne svodi se na osluškivanje vlastitih misli: traži i oblikovanu savjest, istinu i usmjerenost prema dobru.
magisterium.enrichment: Papa Franjo potiče poslovne ljude da se odupru aktivizmu i pronađu vrijeme za promišljanje i kontemplaciju, dok je sveti Grgur Veliki upozoravao da se djelovanje ne poduzima brzopleto, nego uz prethodan savjet i razborito razmatranje. U kršćanskom poduzetništvu savjetovanje i mentorstvo zato imaju smisla kada pomažu odlukama koje poštuju dostojanstvo suradnika i služe zajedničkom dobru, a ne samo osobnom uspjehu.

citations.document_title: To the Members of the “Social Soul in Business Values” Association
Pastoral Rule
To a Delegation of French Catholic entrepreneurs
To representatives of the Union of Industrial Entrepreneurs and Enterprises of Rome (March 18, 2010)

magisterium.assessment_en: The advice on reflecting in silence and seeking prudent counsel is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of responsible action: the Church encourages entrepreneurs to pause, reflect, and make decisions guided by conscience, and not merely by activism or the striving for profit. The passage presents this primarily as a path toward business success, so it would be good to complement it with the discernment of the good, God's will, and the common good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Pope Francis encourages business people to resist activism and find time for reflection and contemplation, while Saint Gregory the Great warned that action should not be undertaken rashly, but with prior counsel and prudent consideration. In Christian entrepreneurship, consultation and mentorship therefore make sense when they assist decisions that respect the dignity of co-workers and serve the common good, not just personal success.
concerns_en: The claim that conversation increases the chance of success can be understood as practical business advice, but it is not a guarantee of success nor a complete Christian criterion for a decision.

The expression that a person in solitude hears himself better is useful for self-reflection, but Catholic discernment is not reduced to listening to one's own thoughts: it also requires a formed conscience, truth, and orientation toward the good.

sections.subtitle_en: One habit, two “little habits”: conversation, getting up early, and silence
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recommends talking with trusted people and morning silence
sections.content_en:
To the question of which habit he would recommend to those starting out in entrepreneurship, Fran says that it is one habit that entails at least two more “sub-habits”. The basic habit is **talking a lot with people in whom you have confidence**, with those who have so far encouraged you and brought you value. One should discuss ideas with them so that they can give additional input. Much communication about one topic, he explains, opens many doors for the plan to be realized in reality. “The more we turn it over, the more the chance increases.”

This also implies a certain pace of life:
- **getting up earlier**,
- **thinking in silence** before the start of work,
- writing out thoughts and bringing them before someone trustworthy.

In silence and solitude, the guest says, a person hears himself much better. First, one needs to become aware of what those thoughts are and why they appear, write them down, and then “put them on the table” before someone and discuss them. Although he admits he complicated it a little, he summarizes: topics should be discussed with those we trust, because that increases the chance of success.

Kruno adds that one should surround oneself with people smarter and more experienced than oneself. People often surround themselves with those who know nothing about their work and who “applaud them here and there”. In fact, **mentors** are needed, from whom one can learn. Fran agrees: “Exactly that.”

sections.subtitle: San iz srednje škole: kršćanski alternativni rock-pop bend
sections.screenshot_description: Fran priča o počecima benda i pomoći don Damira Stojića
sections.content:
Kruno zatim prelazi na još jedan Franov talent, glazbu, i pita kako je nastao bend, što su postigli i kakvi su planovi. Fran kaže da je bend bio njegova srednjoškolska ljubav i „san snova“. Bio je i ostao veliki obožavatelj benda **U2**, koji mu je uvijek bio inspirativan. S vremenom su mu se, kaže, malo udaljili „zbog vrijednosti koje zastupaju“, ali je stara inačica benda bila dobra. Kruno dobacuje: „Dok je trajalo.“

Sve je krenulo iz kreativne podloge. Osjetio je da, kad sjedne za stol s papirom, može napisati rime. Tek je kasnije shvatio koliko se dubokih stvari može staviti u nekoliko rečenica pjesme. Mudrost je, kaže, u tome da se vrijednosti i poruke sažmu u što manje teksta, a vjeruje da je i psalmist imao s tim muke. Fran je završio osnovnu glazbenu školu za klavir, dok je gitaru svladao kao samouk. Uslijedili su prijatelji i zajedničko sviranje pred drugim prijateljima.

Veliki odskok dogodio se prije petnaestak godina, dok je bio u srednjoj školi. Zasluge pripisuje zagrebačkim **salezijancima**, konkretno **don Damiru Stojiću**. On je čuo njihove pjesme, usmjerio ih u studio i potaknuo da traže donacije. Tako su nastale prve pjesme, koje već petnaest godina stoje na **YouTubeu**.

Ideja je bila stvoriti **alternativni rock-pop kršćanski katolički bend**. Projekt je, međutim, financijski zahtjevan i teško ga je pokrenuti, a kamoli održavati dugoročno. Zato Fran objavljuje stvari povremeno, kad su okolnosti povoljne. Cilj je **album od 12 pjesama**, za koji je sav sadržaj gotov, ali se čeka pravi trenutak. Stigla je beba, posao se razvio, pa je hobi morao privremeno ostaviti po strani. Ipak vjeruje da će album biti vrijedan kad izađe.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje kršćansku glazbu kao način izražavanja vjere i vrijednosti, a ne iznosi tvrdnje koje bi bile protivne Svetom pismu ili crkvenom nauku. Budući da se ne navode tekstovi pjesama, nije moguće procijeniti prenose li njihove konkretne poruke cjelovito i točno katolički nauk.
magisterium.enrichment: Sveto pismo potiče kršćane da se izgrađuju psalmima, hvalospjevima i duhovnim pjesmama te da pjevaju Gospodinu iz srca (Ef 5,18–20; Kol 3,16). Katolička tradicija također prepoznaje da glazbeno stvaralaštvo, kada je prožeto vjerom i ljubavlju prema Bogu, može postati izraz štovanja i poticati pobožnost; ipak, glazba namijenjena osobnom ili javnom umjetničkom izrazu nije isto što i liturgijska glazba, za koju vrijede posebni zahtjevi primjerene liturgijskoj svrsi.

citations.document_title: Musicae Sacrae
General Audience of 26 February 2003
25 September 1983: Mass for the Italian Association of St Cecilia - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it portrays Christian music as a way of expressing faith and values, and does not make claims that would be contrary to Sacred Scripture or Church teaching. Since song lyrics are not cited, it is not possible to assess whether their specific messages convey Catholic teaching completely and accurately.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Sacred Scripture encourages Christians to build one another up with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, and to sing to the Lord from the heart (Eph 5:18–20; Col 3:16). Catholic tradition also recognizes that musical creativity, when permeated with faith and love for God, can become an expression of worship and foster devotion; nevertheless, music intended for personal or public artistic expression is not the same as liturgical music, for which special requirements appropriate to its liturgical purpose apply.

sections.subtitle_en: High school dream: a Christian alternative rock-pop band
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about the band's beginnings and the help of don Damir Stojić
sections.content_en:
Kruno then moves on to another of Fran's talents, music, and asks how the band was formed, what they have achieved, and what the plans are. Fran says that the band was his high school love and a "dream of dreams." He was and has remained a big fan of the band **U2**, which was always inspiring to him. Over time, he says, they drifted away from him a bit "because of the values they represent," but the old version of the band was good. Kruno interjects: "While it lasted."

Everything started from a creative foundation. He felt that, when he sits at a table with paper, he can write rhymes. Only later did he realize how many deep things can be put into a few sentences of a song. The wisdom, he says, lies in summarizing values and messages into as little text as possible, and he believes that the psalmist also struggled with that. Fran completed elementary music school for piano, while he mastered the guitar self-taught. Friends followed, along with playing together in front of other friends.

A big leap happened about fifteen years ago, while he was in high school. He attributes credit to the Zagreb **Salesians**, specifically **don Damir Stojić**. He heard their songs, directed them to a studio, and encouraged them to seek donations. That is how the first songs were created, which have been on **YouTube** for fifteen years already.

The idea was to create an **alternative rock-pop Christian Catholic band**. The project is, however, financially demanding and difficult to start, let alone maintain long-term. That is why Fran releases things occasionally, when circumstances are favorable. The goal is an **album of 12 songs**, for which all the content is finished, but the right moment is awaited. A baby arrived, work expanded, so the hobby had to be temporarily set aside. Still, he believes the album will be worthwhile when it comes out.

sections.subtitle: „Stvori me“: pjesma o čovjeku kojega Bog stvara iz pepela
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava poruku svoje najdraže pjesme
sections.content:
Kruno ističe da bi bila šteta ne okruniti sve to „pozitivnim, lijepim, solidnim albumom“ i pita koja je Franu najdraža pjesma. Gost odgovara da je to **„Stvori me“**, koja je bend i „pogurala naprijed među ljude“. Refren ukratko glasi „Stvori me iz pepela“.

Fran objašnjava poruku. Stvarnost je surova i čovjek se često osjeća nebitnim, kao da ga nitko ne doživljava. Proživljava niz neugodnih iskustava s ljudima oko sebe i s društvom, a izvana stiže previše loših informacija, pa se čini da ga svatko želi poniziti. Na kraju se čovjek treba oporaviti i vratiti onome izvornom iz **Knjige Postanka**, gdje Bog stvara čovjeka iz pepela.

Pjesmu je napisao s otprilike 18 godina. Kad ju je nedavno ponovno poslušao, učinila mu se toliko dobrom kao da je nije on napisao. „Čija je to pjesma?“, šali se Kruno, a Fran iskustvo opisuje kao nadrealno, kao čudan déjà vu. Priznaje da mu to nije jedina najdraža pjesma. Još nekoliko pjesama koje tek trebaju izaći bit će mu, kako kaže, „the ones“. Kruno odgovara da jedva čeka, on i supruga, a vjeruje i velika zajednica obožavatelja.

magisterium.assessment: Poruka o obnovi čovjeka nakon poniženja može se čitati kao pjesnička nada u Božje stvarateljsko djelovanje i stoga nije sama po sebi protivna katoličkom nauku. Ipak, tvrdnja da Postanak prikazuje Boga kako stvara čovjeka iz pepela nije biblijski precizna: Post 2,7 govori o prahu zemaljskom i Božjem dahu života, dok se povratak u prah povezuje sa smrtnošću nakon grijeha.
concerns: Miješaju se pepeo, prah i zemlja: pepeo je prikladna pjesnička slika krhkosti ili pokore, ali Post 2,7 ne kaže da je čovjek stvoren od pepela; povezuje ga s prahom zemaljskim i Božjim dahom života.
Izraz „vratiti se onome izvornom“ može zamagliti razliku između stvaranja i posljedica grijeha: u Post 3,19 povratak u prah označava smrtnost, a ne početno stanje čovjeka.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijska slika praha istodobno izražava ljudsku krhkost i ovisnost o Bogu, koji čovjeka oblikuje i daruje mu život; zato čovjek nije bezvrijedan ni slučajan, nego stvoren u Božjem naumu. Pepeo u kršćanskoj uporabi može podsjećati na smrtnost i potrebu obraćenja, ali ne treba ga poistovjetiti s materijalom stvaranja iz Post 2,7. Nada u obnovu dobiva kršćanski smisao u Kristu: smrtnost nije posljednja riječ, jer kršćanska vjera usmjerava prema uskrsnuću i novom životu.

citations.document_title: “What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology
“What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology
“What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology
22 February 2012: "Statio" and Penitential Procession - Holy Mass, Blessing and Imposition of the Ashes
General Audience of 17 February 2010: Ash Wednesday
The Holy Bible
citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: The message of man's renewal after humiliation can be read as a poetic hope in God's creative action and is therefore not in itself contrary to Catholic teaching. However, the claim that Genesis depicts God creating man from ashes is not biblically precise: Gen 2:7 speaks of the dust of the ground and God's breath of life, while the return to dust is associated with mortality after sin.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The biblical image of dust simultaneously expresses human fragility and dependence on God, who shapes man and gives him life; therefore, man is neither worthless nor accidental, but created in God's design. Ashes in Christian usage can serve as a reminder of mortality and the need for conversion, but should not be equated with the material of creation from Gen 2:7. Hope in renewal receives a Christian meaning in Christ: mortality is not the final word, because Christian faith points toward the resurrection and new life.
concerns_en: Ashes, dust, and earth are conflated: ashes are an appropriate poetic image of fragility or penance, but Gen 2:7 does not say that man was created from ashes; it connects him with the dust of the ground and God's breath of life.

The expression "return to that original thing" can obscure the difference between creation and the consequences of sin: in Gen 3:19, the return to dust signifies mortality, not the initial state of man.

sections.subtitle_en: "Create Me": a song about man whom God creates from ashes
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the message of his favorite song
sections.content_en:
Kruno points out that it would be a shame not to crown all this with a "positive, beautiful, solid album" and asks which song is Fran's favorite. The guest replies that it is **"Create Me"**, which also "pushed the band forward among people." The refrain briefly goes "Create me from ashes."

Fran explains the message. Reality is harsh and man often feels insignificant, as if no one notices him. He goes through a series of unpleasant experiences with the people around him and with society, and too much bad information arrives from the outside, so it seems that everyone wants to humiliate him. In the end, man needs to recover and return to that original thing from the **Book of Genesis**, where God creates man from ashes.

He wrote the song when he was about 18 years old. When he listened to it again recently, it seemed so good to him as if he had not written it. "Whose song is that?", Kruno jokes, and Fran describes the experience as surreal, like a strange déjà vu. He admits that this is not his only favorite song. A few more songs that are yet to come out will be, as he says, "the ones" for him. Kruno replies that he can hardly wait, both he and his wife, and he believes a large community of fans as well.

sections.subtitle: S djetetom u naručju na groblju: kako je počela potraga za korijenima
sections.screenshot_description: Fran opisuje trenutak na groblju koji ga je potaknuo na istraživanje porijekla
sections.content:
Kruno spominje Franov velik interes za povijest i njegovo izlaganje na **četvrtoj Konferenciji katoličkih muškaraca u Lovranu**, naslovljeno **„Korijenje prošlosti za plodove budućnosti“**. Ondje je gost predstavio svoju obiteljsku priču. Kruno ga moli da ispriča kako je taj interes počeo i što je otkrio.

Fran kaže da svi odnekud potječemo. Kad čovjek dobije djecu, shvati da će i ona jednog dana dobiti svoju i da tako ide u nedogled, ali i unatrag. Povijest najčešće gledamo kroz političke okolnosti, previranja, ratove i nepravde. Takva povijest zna biti „bez nade“, „šturа i suhoparna“.

Prekretnica je došla nakon rođenja i krštenja jednog od njegove djece. Za **Sve svete** otišao je s djetetom u naručju na groblje i shvatio da dolazi k nekome koga nikad nije upoznao, a tko je „njegov“. Tada je osjetio da mora shvatiti kako su došli do mjesta na kojem jesu. Prezime zvuči germanski i obitelj često zadirkuju da su Nijemci. Zapravo su, otkrit će, podrijetlom **Česi od prije osam generacija**. „Hrvati smo, ali smo davno, davno bili Česi“, pojašnjava.

U mirnijem razdoblju nakon **zagrebačkog potresa** i za vrijeme **korone** javio se ljudima za koje je znao da mu mogu pomoći. Ključan je bio **profesor Vjenceslav Herout**, koji je njegovu ocu predavao u školi još sedamdesetih. On ga je uveo u priču i pokazao mu cijeli svoj opus o tome odakle su ti preci došli, tko su bili i zašto su došli.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na obiteljsku povezanost, sjećanje na pokojne i posjet groblju; pripovjedač opisuje osobno i povijesno istraživanje, a ne zazivanje pokojnika ili traženje nadnaravnih informacija. Ne iznosi izričito teološki nauk, pa ga je primjerenije ocijeniti kao usklađen, a ne kao aktivno produbljivanje katoličkog nauka.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija posjet groblju razumije kao izraz veza između živih i pokojnih, a svetkovina Svih svetih usmjerava pogled prema zajedništvu s Bogom i nadi u život vječni. To se razlikuje od spiritizma: prisjećanje predaka i istraživanje obiteljske povijesti sami po sebi nisu zazivanje duša niti pokušaj da se od njih pribave informacije.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely in alignment with the Catholic view of family connectedness, remembrance of the deceased, and visiting the cemetery; the narrator describes personal and historical research, not the invocation of the deceased or seeking supernatural information. It does not explicitly present theological teaching, so it is more appropriate to assess it as aligned rather than as an active deepening of Catholic teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition understands visiting the cemetery as an expression of bonds between the living and the deceased, and the Solemnity of All Saints directs the gaze toward communion with God and hope in eternal life. This differs from spiritism: remembering ancestors and researching family history are not in themselves the invocation of souls nor an attempt to obtain information from them.

sections.subtitle_en: With a child in arms at the cemetery: how the search for roots began
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran describes the moment at the cemetery that prompted him to research his origins
sections.content_en:
Kruno mentions Fran's great interest in history and his presentation at the **fourth Conference of Catholic Men in Lovran**, entitled **„Roots of the Past for the Fruits of the Future“**. There, the guest presented his family story. Kruno asks him to tell how that interest began and what he discovered.

Fran says that we all come from somewhere. When a person has children, he realizes that they too will have their own one day and that it goes on endlessly like that, but also backwards. We most often look at history through political circumstances, upheavals, wars, and injustices. Such history can be „without hope“, „sparse and dry“.

The turning point came after the birth and baptism of one of his children. For **All Saints**, he went with the child in his arms to the cemetery and realized that he was coming to someone he had never met, but who was „his“. Then he felt that he had to understand how they arrived at the place where they are. The surname sounds Germanic and the family is often teased that they are Germans. In fact, he would discover, they are by origin **Czechs from eight generations ago**. „We are Croats, but we were long, long ago Czechs“, he clarifies.

In the calmer period after the **Zagreb earthquake** and during **corona**, he contacted people he knew could help him. Key was **Professor Vjenceslav Herout**, who taught his father in school back in the seventies. He introduced him to the story and showed him his entire opus about where those ancestors came from, who they were, and why they came.
entities_en: Roots of the Past for the Fruits of the Future

sections.subtitle: Graničari, pješaci i obiteljska kronika koja pamti i bake
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava značenje prezimena i češke pretke graničare
sections.content:
Istraživanje je pokazalo da su Franovi preci bili **graničari** u vrijeme borbi s Turcima. Kad je Slavonija postupno oslobođena, pozivani su ljudi koji će ondje stražariti. Došlo je oko **petsto Čeha**, cijelo selo, a kao protuvrijednost za čuvanje granice dobili su zemlju. Upoznajući sve više stručnjaka, Fran je istraživanje doveo do **kasnog srednjeg vijeka**, „od djeda do djeda“.

Otkrio je i značenje prezimena, koje nema uporište u hrvatskom, nego u njemačkom jeziku, a značilo je **„pješak, vojnik“**. Ta mu je simbolika draga iz tri razloga. Takav je izvor prezimena, preci su bili graničari, a danas se i sam osjeća kao da brani dostojanstvo svoje obitelji i domovine u kojoj i za koju živi. Zato smatra da bi svatko trebao otkriti svoje korijene. Upozorava ipak da to traži „užasno puno vremena“ i da nije preporučljivo mladima. On je, kaže, imao taj luksuz.

Plod istraživanja bit će **interna obiteljska knjiga**, opsežna kronika koja neće biti javna, a pojasnit će odakle je obitelj potekla. Posebnost je u tome što nije istraživao samo očevu lozu. Popisao je **sve žene**, i s majčine i sa svoje strane, jer je htio znati koje su bake postojale prije njega. Sada ima kćeri i želi i njima to ispričati.

Veliku inspiraciju bila mu je **pokojna prabaka**. Pričala mu je o svojim bakama rođenima 1840-ih, kojih se sjećala. Franu je nevjerojatno da mu netko tko je živio u njegovo vrijeme može pričati o ljudima od prije 170 godina, iz **doba Jelačića**, kao da je bilo jučer. To vidi kao crtu koja spaja nebo i zemlju.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na obiteljsku pripadnost, poštovanje predaka i prenošenje obiteljske povijesti, a istraživanje podrijetla samo po sebi ne predstavlja teološki problem. Izraz da prabaka povezuje nebo i zemlju najbolje je razumjeti kao poetsku sliku međugeneracijske bliskosti, a ne kao tvrdnju o komunikaciji s pokojnicima.
concerns: Izraz „crta koja spaja nebo i zemlju” mogao bi biti nejasan ako bi se shvatio kao tvrdnja da pokojni izravno prenose poruke ili informacije; odlomak to, međutim, ne tvrdi.

Govorenje o obrani obiteljskog i domovinskog dostojanstva može biti legitimno, ali ne bi smjelo voditi isključivosti, omalovažavanju drugih naroda ili poistovjećivanju domoljublja s kršćanskom vjerom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija vrednuje čuvanje sjećanja na pretke i obiteljske baštine te potiče molitvu za pokojne i u zajedništvu s njima, ali razlikuje takvo sjećanje i molitvu od zazivanja mrtvih radi dobivanja skrivenih informacija. Biblijske genealogije pokazuju da obiteljsko podrijetlo može imati značenje za razumijevanje povijesti i pripadnosti, dok istodobno usmjeravaju pozornost na Božje djelovanje u ljudskoj povijesti. Uključivanje ženskih predaka također je u skladu s cjelovitim prikazom obitelji: obiteljska se povijest ne svodi na jednu lozu, nego pamti osobe i odnose koji su oblikovali naraštaje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely in alignment with the Catholic view on family belonging, respect for ancestors, and the transmission of family history, and the investigation of origins in itself does not present a theological problem. The expression that the great-grandmother connects heaven and earth is best understood as a poetic image of intergenerational closeness, rather than as an assertion of communication with the deceased.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition values preserving the memory of ancestors and family heritage, and encourages prayer for the deceased and in communion with them, but it distinguishes such remembrance and prayer from evoking the dead to obtain hidden information. Biblical genealogies show that family origin can have significance for understanding history and belonging, while simultaneously directing attention to God's action in human history. The inclusion of female ancestors is also in accordance with an integral depiction of the family: family history is not reduced to a single lineage, but remembers the persons and relationships that shaped generations.
concerns_en: The expression “a line connecting heaven and earth” could be unclear if understood as a claim that the deceased directly transmit messages or information; the passage, however, does not claim this.
Speaking of defending family and homeland dignity can be legitimate, but it should not lead to exclusivity, belittling other nations, or equating patriotism with the Christian faith.

sections.subtitle_en: Frontiersmen, foot soldiers, and a family chronicle that also remembers grandmothers
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the meaning of the surname and Czech frontiersman ancestors
sections.content_en:
Research showed that Fran's ancestors were **frontiersmen** at the time of the battles with the Turks. When Slavonija was gradually liberated, people were summoned who would keep watch there. Around **five hundred Czechs** arrived, an entire village, and as compensation for guarding the border they received land. Getting to know more and more experts, Fran brought the research up to the **Late Middle Ages**, “from grandfather to grandfather”.

He also discovered the meaning of the surname, which has no basis in Croatian, but in German, and it meant **“foot soldier, soldier”**. That symbolism is dear to him for three reasons. Such is the origin of the surname, the ancestors were frontiersmen, and today he himself feels as though he is defending the dignity of his family and the homeland in which and for which he lives. That is why he believes everyone should discover their roots. He warns, however, that this takes “an awful lot of time” and that it is not recommended for young people. He, he says, had that luxury.

The fruit of the research will be an **internal family book**, an extensive chronicle that will not be public, and will clarify where the family came from. The distinctiveness is that he did not investigate only his father's lineage. He cataloged **all the women**, both on his mother's side and on his own, because he wanted to know which grandmothers existed before him. Now he has daughters and wants to tell them this too.

A great inspiration to him was his **late great-grandmother**. She spoke to him about her grandmothers born in the 1840s, whom she remembered. It is incredible to Fran that someone who lived in his time can tell him about people from 170 years ago, from the **era of Jelačić**, as if it were yesterday. He sees that as a line connecting heaven and earth.

sections.subtitle: Demokracija živih i mrtvih: svi smo braća i sestre
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o Bogu Ocu kao izvoru i povezanosti svih Hrvata
sections.content:
Fran se ponovno poziva na **Chestertona**, koji je rekao da živimo u „demokraciji neba i zemlje, odnosno živih i mrtvih“. Treba osvijestiti da Crkvu čine i oni koji su ovdje i oni koji su na nebu, „daj Bože da i mi jednog dana“. Smatra to nužnim dijelom razumijevanja vlastitog identiteta za svakoga tko može ići tim putem.

Najveće otkriće cijelog istraživanja, kaže gost, bilo je da je izvor svih tih ljudi zapravo **Bog Otac** i da smo ukorijenjeni u njemu. To znači da smo **svi braća i sestre**. Kad to shvati, čovjeku se automatski mijenja pristup drugima jer zna da je svakome „nešto u nekom tamo koljenu“.

Za Hrvate to posebno vrijedi. Po Franovu mišljenju svi smo rođaci „u petnaestom, šesnaestom koljenu“ jer smo premalen narod da bismo bili nepovezani. Navodi primjere:
- Slavonija je puna Hercegovaca,
- Lika je puna Bosanaca,
- Dubrovnik je pun ljudi iz srednje Bosne.

Svi smo, zaključuje, „drevno izmiješan narod“, i to je dobro jer zbog toga možemo biti bolji i bliži. Kruno dodaje: „Svi smo braća i sestre u Kristu.“ Fran potvrđuje: „U Kristu, na kraju krajeva.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: Crkva doista obuhvaća vjernike na zemlji i one koji su u nebu, a kršćansko bratstvo ukorijenjeno je u Bogu i Kristu. Potrebno je ipak razlikovati opće ljudsko bratstvo, utemeljeno na zajedničkom Stvoritelju, od posebnog bratstva u Kristu koje pripada zajedništvu vjernika.
concerns: Tvrdnja da su svi Hrvati rođaci u petnaestom ili šesnaestom koljenu iznesena je kao procjena, a ne kao utvrđena činjenica; nije teološki nauk.
Izraz „svi smo braća i sestre” može biti nejasan ako se ne razlikuje opće ljudsko bratstvo od posinjenja u Kristu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katekizam uči da vjernici na zemlji, pokojni koji se čiste i blaženi u nebu zajedno tvore jednu Crkvu, pa je spominjanje živih i preminulih dobro povezano sa zajedništvom svetih. Kršćansko jedinstvo nije samo osjećaj zajedničkog podrijetla nego dar Kristove milosti, koji se konkretno očituje u ljubavi i služenju; zemaljske i narodne veze imaju vrijednost, ali ih Krist otvara prema širem zajedništvu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: the Church indeed encompasses the faithful on earth and those who are in heaven, and Christian brotherhood is rooted in God and Christ. It is necessary, however, to distinguish general human brotherhood, based on a common Creator, from the special brotherhood in Christ that belongs to the communion of the faithful.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catechism teaches that the faithful on earth, the deceased who are being purified, and the blessed in heaven together form one Church, so the mention of the living and the deceased is well connected with the communion of saints. Christian unity is not merely a feeling of common origin but a gift of Christ's grace, which is concretely manifested in love and service; earthly and national ties have value, but Christ opens them toward a broader communion.
concerns_en: The claim that all Croats are relatives in the fifteenth or sixteenth generation was presented as an estimate, not as an established fact; it is not theological teaching.
The expression „we are all brothers and sisters” can be unclear if general human brotherhood is not distinguished from adoption in Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: Democracy of the living and the dead: we are all brothers and sisters
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran speaks about God the Father as the source and the interconnectedness of all Croats
sections.content_en:
Fran refers once again to **Chesterton**, who said that we live in a „democracy of heaven and earth, that is, of the living and the dead”. One should become aware that the Church is made up of both those who are here and those who are in heaven, „God grant that we may be one day too”. He considers this a necessary part of understanding one's own identity for anyone who can walk that path.

The greatest discovery of the entire research, the guest says, was that the source of all those people is actually **God the Father** and that we are rooted in him. This means that **we are all brothers and sisters**. When a person realizes this, their approach to others automatically changes because they know that they are „something to everyone in some distant generation”.

This is especially true for Croats. In Fran's opinion, we are all relatives „in the fifteenth, sixteenth generation” because we are too small a nation to be unconnected. He cites examples:
- Slavonija is full of Herzegovinians,
- Lika is full of Bosnians,
- Dubrovnik is full of people from central Bosnia.

We are all, he concludes, an „anciently mixed nation”, and that is good because of that we can be better and closer. Kruno adds: „We are all brothers and sisters in Christ.” Fran confirms: „In Christ, after all.”

sections.subtitle: 1360 prezimena koja su prošla ispod radara
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Kruno govori o svojoj knjizi o prezimenima i slabom interesu javnosti
sections.content:
Kruno otkriva da ga je razočaralo što mnoge ljude ta tema ne zanima. Deset godina radio je na doktoratu koji se, između ostalog, bavi imenima i prezimenima njegova kraja, **Poklončićkog prigorja**. Iz rada je nastala i knjiga **„Prezimena Poklončićkog prigorja“**. Mislio je da će je ljudi „razgrabiti“. Nije računao na zaradu, nego na interes. Knjiga je ipak „prošla ispod radara“: tek tu i tamo netko pita za nju ili pogleda svoje prezime.

U knjizi je obradio **1360 prezimena**, s prvom pojavom, grafijom, značenjem, etimologijom i motivacijom. Prezimena su, kaže, toliko zanimljiva i toliko toga govore, a mnoge „nije briga“. Kruno smatra da čovjek mora znati odakle je došao jer to na neki način pokazuje i kamo ide. Podrijetlo ne zacrtava put, ali je velik poticaj. Ipak, Franova i druge slične priče ohrabruju ga da nije pisao samo za sebe.

Fran upozorava na fenomen u **Americi**, gdje raste cijeli val istraživača **genealogije**. Ondje su svi odnekud došli, a mnogi ne znaju odakle. Vjeruje da će se to postupno dogoditi i u Hrvatskoj jer svi mislimo da smo „samo“ ono što jesmo. On je mislio da su mu svi preci Slavonci, a ispostavilo se da su Česi. „Svi smo odnekuda.“

Iz istraživanja je izvukao i veliku lekciju. Treba se ponositi podrijetlom, ali **ne površno**. Svaki rod nosi svoj teret, pa i „grijehe starine“. S druge strane, ne treba ni živjeti pod tim bremenom jer na davna vremena više ne možemo utjecati. Ono što možemo jest zahvaliti Bogu za svakoga tko je postojao i dopustio da se rodi sljedeći, sve do nas. Da samo jedna osoba nije bila u tom lancu, „nas vjerojatno ne bi bilo“. To je, kaže gost, čudo, i upravo zato vrijedi istražiti tko je sve bio prije nas.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom snažno usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na obiteljsku povijest: potiče zahvalnost, čuvanje sjećanja i poniznost, a izričito kaže da podrijetlo ne zacrtava čovjekov životni put. Izraz o teretu i grijesima predaka traži samo pojašnjenje da se nasljeđuju posljedice i povijesna povezanost, a ne osobna krivnja predaka.
concerns: Izraz da svaki rod nosi grijehe starine može se pogrešno shvatiti kao da potomci osobno snose krivnju za grijehe predaka; katolički je prikladnije razlikovati osobnu odgovornost od povijesnih posljedica i međugeneracijske povezanosti.

Tvrdnja da nas vjerojatno ne bi bilo da je jedna osoba iz lanca izostala razumljiva je kao opažanje o konkretnom obiteljskom podrijetlu, ali ne treba je pretvoriti u tvrdnju da je svaka povijesna okolnost bila moralno dobra ili nužna.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijske genealogije nisu samo popisi podrijetla: one prikazuju povijest ljudskih naraštaja u kojoj je Bog prisutan i vodi događaje prema blagoslovu, a biblijski rodoslovlja u konačnici usmjeravaju pozornost na Krista i povijest spasenja. Crkveno promišljanje priznaje solidarnost među naraštajima u dobru i zlu te mogućnost kajanja za grijehe prošlosti, ali to nije isto što i pripisati potomku osobnu krivnju za tuđi čin. Čuvanje uspomene na pretke može biti izraz zahvalnosti i brige za obiteljske korijene, uz slobodu svakoga naraštaja da odgovorno oblikuje budućnost.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely strongly aligned with the Catholic view of family history: it encourages gratitude, the preservation of memory, and humility, and explicitly states that origin does not plot a person's life path. The expression regarding the burden and sins of ancestors requires only the clarification that consequences and historical connectedness are inherited, not the personal guilt of ancestors.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical genealogies are not merely lists of origin: they depict the history of human generations in which God is present and guides events toward blessing, and biblical genealogies ultimately direct attention to Christ and the history of salvation. Ecclesial reflection recognizes solidarity among generations in good and evil and the possibility of repentance for the sins of the past, but that is not the same as attributing to a descendant personal guilt for another's deed. Preserving the memory of ancestors can be an expression of gratitude and care for family roots, alongside the freedom of every generation to responsibly shape the future.
concerns_en: The expression that every lineage carries the sins of old can be misunderstood as if descendants personally bear guilt for the sins of ancestors; from a Catholic perspective, it is more appropriate to distinguish personal responsibility from historical consequences and intergenerational connectedness.

The claim that we probably would not exist if one person from the chain had been missing is understandable as an observation about concrete family origin, but it should not be turned into a claim that every historical circumstance was morally good or necessary.

sections.subtitle_en: 1360 surnames that passed under the radar
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Kruno talks about his book on surnames and the weak public interest
sections.content_en:
Kruno reveals that it disappointed him that many people are not interested in this topic. For ten years he worked on a doctorate which, among other things, deals with the first names and surnames of his region, **Poklončićko prigorje**. From this work, the book **“Prezimena Poklončićkog prigorja”** also came about. He thought that people would “snap it up.” He was not counting on profit, but on interest. The book nonetheless “passed under the radar”: only here and there does someone ask about it or look up their surname.

In the book, he covered **1360 surnames**, with first occurrence, orthography, meaning, etymology, and motivation. Surnames are, he says, so interesting and say so much, and many “do not care.” Kruno believes that a person must know where he came from because in a way that also shows where he is going. Origin does not plot the path, but it is a great incentive. Still, Fran's and other similar stories encourage him that he was not writing only for himself.

Fran warns of a phenomenon in **America**, where an entire wave of **genealogy** researchers is growing. There everyone came from somewhere, and many do not know from where. He believes that this will gradually happen in Croatia as well because we all think that we are “only” what we are. He thought that all his ancestors were Slavonians, and it turned out that they are Czechs. “We are all from somewhere.”

From the research he also drew a great lesson. One should be proud of one's origin, but **not superficially**. Every lineage carries its own burden, even “sins of old.” On the other hand, one should not live under that burden either, because we can no longer influence ancient times. What we can do is thank God for everyone who existed and allowed the next one to be born, all the way to us. If only one person had not been in that chain, “we probably would not exist.” That is, says the guest, a miracle, and precisely because of that it is worth researching everyone who came before us.

sections.subtitle: Prijatelj koji je nakon 25 godina stao na očev grob
sections.screenshot_description: Fran prepričava dirljivu priču o prijatelju koji je pronašao oca
sections.content:
Fran dijeli i „friški događaj“. Nedavno je upoznao čovjeka koji ga je dočekao u jednom mjestu. Kad mu je rekao kako se preziva, Fran je odgovorio: „Čovječe, pa moja se šukunbaka tako prezivala.“ Pitao ga je je li iz tog i tog kraja, i bio je. Novi poznanik priznao mu je da ima složenu situaciju. To je majčino prezime, a oca nikad nije upoznao. Majka o tome nije voljela govoriti, a njega je to mučilo cijeli život, više od 25 godina.

Fran mu je rekao što bi sam napravio na njegovu mjestu, jer ima neke resurse. Nakon tri mjeseca prijatelj mu se javio: „Slušaj, bio sam prekjučer na grobu svog oca.“ Oca je pronašao u **drugoj državi**. Saznao je njegovo ime i prezime i prvi put u životu vidio ljude koji nalikuju na njega i nose isto prezime.

Gost priznaje da je nakon toga bio dva dana pod dojmom. Netko je zbog njihova razgovora smogao snage otići toliko daleko, u drugu državu, da otkrije istinu. Tu je ponovno vidio koliko je važno otkriti identitet za kojim je netko tragao cijeli život, „barem taj zemaljski identitet“.

Kruno zaključuje da je **identitet** jedno od najvažnijih pitanja čovječanstva. Kad čovjek sazna tko je, to mu je „velik vjetar u leđa“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem čovjeka: prepoznaje da potraga za podrijetlom može biti duboko važna za osobni identitet i dostojanstvo. Ipak, izraz „zemaljski identitet” ostaje nedorečen, pa bi bilo korisno naznačiti da obiteljsko podrijetlo jest važan dio identiteta, ali nije njegov konačni temelj ni mjera čovjekove vrijednosti.
concerns: Moglo bi se steći dojam da se čovjekovo samorazumijevanje ili vrijednost prvenstveno temelje na pronalasku oca i biološkoj obitelji; katolički nauk, međutim, u konačnici utemeljuje identitet u tome da je osoba stvorenje i ljubljeno dijete Božje, dok njezino dostojanstvo ne ovisi o obiteljskim okolnostima.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijski rodoslovi pokazuju da obiteljsko podrijetlo ima važno mjesto u razumijevanju osobe, a Sveto pismo ne spominje samo očeve nego i majke te njihovu ulogu u povijesti potomstva. Kršćanski pogled istodobno nadilazi biološki rodoslov: najdublji identitet čovjeka jest poziv na sinovstvo i kćerinstvo pred Bogom, a ljudsko dostojanstvo ostaje neotuđivo neovisno o njegovim obiteljskim okolnostima.

Nevertheless, the expression "earthly identity" remains incomplete, so it would be helpful to indicate that family origin is an important part of identity, but not its ultimate foundation nor the measure of human worth.

sections.subtitle_en: A friend who, after 25 years, stood at his father's grave
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran recounts a touching story about a friend who found his father
sections.content_en:
Fran also shares a "fresh event". Recently, he met a man who welcomed him in a certain place. When he told him what his last name was, Fran replied: "Man, that was my great-great-grandmother's last name." He asked him if he was from that and that region, and he was. The new acquaintance admitted to him that he had a complex situation. That was his mother's last name, and he had never met his father. His mother did not like to talk about it, and it had troubled him his entire life, for more than 25 years.

Fran told him what he would do in his place, because he had some resources. After three months, the friend contacted him: "Listen, the day before yesterday I was at my father's grave." He found his father in **another country**. He learned his first and last name and, for the first time in his life, saw people who look like him and bear the same last name.

The guest admits that after that he was deeply moved for two days. Because of their conversation, someone had gathered the strength to go so far, to another country, to discover the truth. There he saw once again how important it is to discover an identity that someone has searched for their whole life, "at least that earthly identity".

Kruno concludes that **identity** is one of humanity's most important questions. When a person finds out who they are, that gives them "a great wind at their back".

sections.subtitle: Blic „ili-ili“, „Ne bojte se!“ i poruka nade za kraj
sections.screenshot_description: Gost preporučuje knjigu i upućuje poruku mladim muškarcima
sections.content:
Pred kraj Kruno uvodi „blitzkrieg“ pet kratkih **„ili-ili“ pitanja**. Napominje da su neka „tricky“, a neka možda i komična, te da gost slobodno smije odbiti obje opcije. Franovi odgovori:
- **Inspiracija ili disciplina?** Inspiracija.
- **Raditi noću ili ujutro?** Ujutro.
- **Božja pobjeda ili Prdavci?** Uz uzvik „O, čovječe!“ i šalu da ovisi o okolnostima, Božja pobjeda. Kruno to komentira kao „mudro“.
- **Sestre Halužan ili sestre Palić?** Sestre Halužan, iz sentimentalnih razloga, jer su mu bile „desne ruke“ na snimanju pjesme. Dodaje da se sestre Palić ne trebaju uvrijediti jer ga „Kornelija i ekipa“ dobro znaju. Kruno gledatelje poziva da pogledaju spot.
- **Kreativni kaos ili uredna struktura?** Kreativni kaos.

Za kraj Kruno traži poruku mladim muškarcima bilo kojeg poziva koji imaju snove, ali se boje odvažiti. Fran preporučuje knjigu **„Sanjajte i snovi će nadići realnost“**. Napisao ju je prijatelj **svetog Josemaríje Escrive**, a temelji se na istinitom događaju. Govori o poticajima koje je Escrivá imao prije osnivanja **Opusa Dei**, Djela Božjeg. Djelo je nastalo iz jedne ideje u razmatranju, a danas je, kako kaže Fran, velika struktura u Crkvi i „dobra kičma muževnosti u Crkvi“. Svoju poruku sažima riječima pape **Ivana Pavla II.**: **„Ne bojte se!“** Kruno dodaje „Uzmi i čitaj“, a gost se slaže.

Kruno zahvaljuje gostu na svjedočanstvu i bogatom iskustvu za koje vjeruje da je progovorilo mnogima. Fran zahvaljuje na pozivu i poželi da svaki podcast bude „ovako slojevit i šaljiv na kraju“. Voditelj se zatim oprašta od publike i poziva je da podcast podrže na **Patreonu**, gdje mogu već danas pogledati sljedeću epizodu.

Nakon odjave slijedi kratak isječak s porukom nade: **„Nisi sam. Nisi sam i može biti bolje.“** U njemu se ističe da je mnogima bolje nego prije, nakon što su prošli program, i da nitko od onih koji su ga prošli nije zažalio, nego su „našli mir“.

magisterium.assessment: Poruka da se čovjek ne prepusti strahu nego s nadom i hrabrošću krene za svojim pozivom uglavnom je u skladu s kršćanskim naukom; jednako je katolički naglasak da se svetost može živjeti u svakodnevnom radu i životnim okolnostima. Ipak, tvrdnju da je Opus Dei „dobra kičma muževnosti u Crkvi“ valja shvatiti kao osobno vrednovanje, a ne kao službeno crkveno učenje ili jedini uzor kršćanske muževnosti.
concerns: Izraz „dobra kičma muževnosti u Crkvi“ može zvučati kao opća tvrdnja o ulozi Opusa Dei ili o tome što znači kršćanska muževnost; sam odlomak ne pojašnjava tu ocjenu.
Poruka „može biti bolje“ i tvrdnja da nitko nije požalio nakon sudjelovanja u neimenovanom programu mogu biti ohrabrujuće svjedočanstvo, ali ne treba ih razumjeti kao jamstvo ishoda za svakoga.
Opis nastanka Opusa Dei kao ideje u razmatranju ne treba tumačiti tako da zanemaruje razlučivanje poziva, molitvu i crkvenu vjernost.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćansko „Ne bojte se“ ne znači da vjernik nikad ne osjeća strah niti da treba nepromišljeno riskirati: crkveni nauk priznaje stvarnost straha te potiče na razlučivanje, molitvu i postupno otkrivanje poziva. Učenje povezano s Opusom Dei naglašava opći poziv na svetost i mogućnost da se svakodnevni, pošteni rad živi kao put posvećenja i apostolata; to nije tvrdnja da je samo jedan životni put ili duhovnost prikladan za sve.

magisterium.assessment_en: The message that one should not surrender to fear but pursue one's vocation with hope and courage is broadly in line with Christian teaching; equally Catholic is the emphasis that holiness can be lived in everyday work and life circumstances. Nevertheless, the claim that Opus Dei is a “good backbone of masculinity in the Church” should be understood as a personal assessment, not as official Church teaching or the sole model of Christian masculinity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Christian “Do not be afraid” does not mean that a believer never feels fear or should take reckless risks: Church teaching recognizes the reality of fear and encourages discernment, prayer, and the gradual discovery of one's vocation. The teaching associated with Opus Dei emphasizes the universal call to holiness and the possibility of living everyday, honest work as a path of sanctification and apostolate; this is not a claim that only one path of life or spirituality is suitable for everyone.
concerns_en: The expression “good backbone of masculinity in the Church” may sound like a general claim about the role of Opus Dei or about what Christian masculinity means; the passage itself does not clarify this assessment.

The message “it can get better” and the claim that no one regretted participating in the unnamed program may be an encouraging testimony, but they should not be understood as a guarantee of outcome for everyone.
The description of the emergence of Opus Dei as an idea in meditation should not be interpreted in a way that disregards vocational discernment, prayer, and ecclesial fidelity.

sections.subtitle_en: Blitz “either-or”, “Do not be afraid!” and a message of hope for the end
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recommends a book and addresses a message to young men
sections.content_en:
Near the end, Kruno introduces a “blitzkrieg” of five short **“either-or” questions**. He notes that some are “tricky”, and some perhaps comical, and that the guest is freely allowed to reject both options. Fran's answers:
- **Inspiration or discipline?** Inspiration.
- **Working at night or in the morning?** In the morning.
- **Božja pobjeda or Prdavci?** With an exclamation “Oh, man!” and a joke that it depends on the circumstances, Božja pobjeda. Kruno comments on this as “wise”.
- **Sestre Halužan or sestre Palić?** Sestre Halužan, for sentimental reasons, because they were his “right-hand women” during the song recording. He adds that sestre Palić should not be offended because “Kornelija and the crew” know him well. Kruno invites the viewers to watch the music video.
- **Creative chaos or orderly structure?** Creative chaos.

For the end, Kruno asks for a message to young men of any vocation who have dreams, but are afraid to dare. Fran recommends the book **“Dream and dreams will surpass reality”**. It was written by a friend of **Saint Josemaría Escrivá**, and is based on a true event. It speaks about the inspirations Escrivá had before founding **Opus Dei**, the Work of God. The Work arose from an idea in meditation, and today, as Fran says, it is a large structure in the Church and a “good backbone of masculinity in the Church”. He summarizes his message with the words of Pope **John Paul II**: **“Do not be afraid!”** Kruno adds “Take and read”, and the guest agrees.

Kruno thanks the guest for his testimony and rich experience, which he believes spoke to many. Fran thanks him for the invitation and wishes that every podcast would be “this layered and humorous at the end”. The host then bids farewell to the audience and invites them to support the podcast on **Patreon**, where they can already watch the next episode today.

After the sign-off, a short clip follows with a message of hope: **“You are not alone. You are not alone and it can get better.”** In it, it is emphasized that many are doing better than before, after having gone through the program, and that none of those who went through it regretted it, but rather “found peace”.
